lessons.title: 47. Review: greetings and introductions
lessons.subtitle: Meeting, asking, nationality, languages and numbers

explanations.title: What you have covered
explanations.body: You can now greet someone, ask and give names, ask whether someone is a student or teacher, ask who someone is, introduce a third person, say what nationality and languages people have, and ask for a phone number. The questions below mix all of this.

examples.text: 您好！请问，您贵姓？
examples.translation: nín hǎo! qǐngwèn, nín guìxìng — Hello! May I ask your surname?

examples.text: 这位是我的朋友，他是美国人，也说中文。
examples.translation: zhèwèi shì wǒ de péngyou, tā shì Měiguó rén, yě shuō Zhōngwén — This is my friend. He is American and also speaks Chinese.

examples.text: 对了，你的手机号码是多少？
examples.translation: duìle, nǐ de shǒujī hàomǎ shì duōshǎo — By the way, what is your cell phone number?

exercises.prompt: Which turns a statement into a yes/no question?
exercises.explanation: 吗 goes on the end of a statement.

exercises.prompt: Which is the polite form of “you”?
Which question asks for a person?

exercises.explanation: Before a 4th tone it is bú.

units.title: 第三课 Family and work

lessons.title: 48. Having: 有 and 没有
lessons.subtitle: 我有妹妹 · 我没有哥哥 · 你有姐姐吗？

explanations.title: 有 means “to have”
explanations.body: 有 is the verb for having and owning: 我有妹妹, “I have a younger sister”. It is also how Chinese says “there is” or “there are”. Its negative is 没有 (méiyǒu), never 不有. In a short answer, 没有 can stand alone, and 没 is méi, in the 2nd tone. To ask a yes/no question, add 吗, as always.

rows: I do not have an older brother.
Do you have an older sister?

explanations.title: Question and answer
explanations.body: Answer with 有 for “yes” and 没有 for “no”, then add the detail if you like. 我们家 means “our family” or “our home”.

examples.text: 你有弟弟吗？ 有，我有一个弟弟。
examples.translation: nǐ yǒu dìdi ma? yǒu, wǒ yǒu yí gè dìdi — Do you have a younger brother? Yes, I have one.

examples.text: 你有姐姐吗？ 没有，我有哥哥。
examples.translation: nǐ yǒu jiějie ma? méiyǒu, wǒ yǒu gēge — Do you have an older sister? No, I have an older brother.

examples.text: 我们家有五口人。
examples.translation: wǒmen jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén — My family has five people.

examples.text: 他没有孩子。
examples.translation: tā méiyǒu háizi — He has no children.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 没有?
What is the negative of 有?
exercises.explanation: 有 is negated with 没, not 不: 没有.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “I do not have an older brother”?
What does 我有妹妹 mean?
exercises.explanation: 有 is have; 妹妹 is a younger sister.

options: Do you have a younger sister?
Do you have an older sister?

Do you have an older sister?

lessons.title: 49. Family members
lessons.subtitle: 爷爷, 奶奶, 哥哥, 姐姐, 弟弟, 妹妹

explanations.title: Older and younger
explanations.body: Chinese has separate words for older and younger siblings, so you always say which one you mean: 哥哥 is an older brother and 弟弟 a younger brother, 姐姐 an older sister and 妹妹 a younger sister. 兄弟姐妹 gathers them all: “brothers and sisters”, siblings. 爷爷 and 奶奶 are your father's father and mother, and they are the words people use at home. In each of these words the second syllable is neutral, except in 兄弟姐妹.

explanations.title: Birth order and family photos
explanations.body: To say which older sibling, put 大 (eldest), 二 (second) or 三 (third) before the word: 大哥 is the eldest brother, 二姐 the second older sister. To show a photo, say 你看, “look”, and use 照片, which means a photo, and 家, which means family or home.

explanations.title: In a conversation
explanations.body: Here is how it sounds when someone shows a family photo.

examples.text: 你看，这是我们家的照片。
examples.translation: nǐ kàn, zhè shì wǒmen jiā de zhàopiàn — Look, this is a photo of our family.

examples.text: 这是你哥哥吗？ 不是，这是我弟弟。
examples.translation: zhè shì nǐ gēge ma? búshì, zhè shì wǒ dìdi — Is this your older brother? No, this is my younger brother.

examples.text: 这是你大姐吗？ 不是，这是我二姐。
examples.translation: zhè shì nǐ dàjiě ma? búshì, zhè shì wǒ èrjiě — Is this your eldest sister? No, this is my second sister.

exercises.prompt: What does 兄弟姐妹 mean?
How do you read 哥哥?
How do you read 弟弟?
How do you read 奶奶?
How do you read 爷爷?
How do you read 兄弟姐妹?
exercises.explanation: 兄弟姐妹 is read xiōngdì jiěmèi.

exercises.prompt: Which word is an older sister?
exercises.explanation: 姐 is older sister; 妹 is younger.

exercises.prompt: What does 大 mean in 大哥?
exercises.explanation: 大哥 is the eldest brother.
弟弟 is a younger brother.
exercises.promptTranslation: This is my younger brother.
Look, this is a photo of our family.

lessons.title: 50. Numbers 11 to 99, and 二 against 两
lessons.subtitle: 十一, 二十, 三十五 · 两个

explanations.title: Building the tens
explanations.body: Numbers above ten are built like a sum. 十一 is “ten-one” (11), 十二 is “ten-two” (12), and so on up to 十九. Twenty is 二十, “two-ten”, and 二十一 is “two-ten-one” (21). 三十五 is “three-ten-five” (35). The same pattern runs to 九十九.

explanations.title: 二 and 两
explanations.body: Both mean “two”. Use 二 for counting, for digits and for the number itself: 一、二、三, 十二, 二十. Use 两 before a measure word or a noun, to say how many: 两个姐姐 is “two older sisters”. You do not say 二个. In the word 二哥 the 二 is a position in the family, not a quantity, so it stays 二.

examples.text: 二十二岁
examples.translation: èrshíèr suì — twenty-two years old

examples.text: 我有两个姐姐。
examples.translation: wǒ yǒu liǎng gè jiějie — I have two older sisters.

examples.text: 我们家有两口人。
examples.translation: wǒmen jiā yǒu liǎng kǒu rén — There are two people in our family.

examples.text: 这是我二哥。
examples.translation: zhè shì wǒ èrgē — This is my second older brother.

exercises.explanation: 三十五 is three tens and five.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 十二?
How do you read 三十五?
How do you read 九十九?
Which is correct for “two older sisters”?
exercises.explanation: Use 两 before a measure word.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct for “two people in the family”?
Why is 二姐 not 两姐?
options: 二 shows position in the family
exercises.explanation: 二姐 is “second older sister”: a position, not a quantity.
两 comes before the measure word 个.
exercises.promptTranslation: I have two older sisters.
I am 22 years old.

lessons.title: 51. Measure words and 几
lessons.subtitle: 一个, 五口, 三位 · 几口人？

explanations.title: A measure word between number and noun
explanations.body: In Chinese a number or 这/那 cannot sit directly in front of a noun: a measure word goes between them, like “a slice of bread” in English. Every noun has its own measure word, so learn them together. Three are enough for now: 个 is the general one (一个哥哥), 口 counts the members of a family (五口人) and 位 counts people respectfully (三位老师).

explanations.title: 几 asks “how many?”
explanations.body: 几 asks for a number, usually from one to nine, and it takes a measure word too: 你有几个姐姐？ The answer simply takes the place of 几. For a number that could be larger than ten, use 多少.

examples.text: 你们家有几口人？
examples.translation: nǐmen jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén — How many people are there in your family?

examples.text: 我们家有七口人。
examples.translation: wǒmen jiā yǒu qī kǒu rén — There are seven in our family.

examples.text: 你有几个姐姐？ 我有两个。
examples.translation: nǐ yǒu jǐ gè jiějie? wǒ yǒu liǎng gè — How many older sisters do you have? I have two.

examples.text: 你们班有几位老师？
examples.translation: nǐmen bān yǒu jǐ wèi lǎoshī — How many teachers does your class have?

exercises.explanation: 口 (kǒu) means “(measure word for family members)”.

exercises.prompt: Where does the measure word go?
options: Between the number and the noun

exercises.prompt: Which measure word counts members of a family?
exercises.explanation: 五口人: five in a family.

exercises.prompt: Which measure word is respectful, for people?
Which is the most general measure word?
How do you say “three teachers” respectfully?
How do you say “five people in a family”?

exercises.promptTranslation: There are five people in our family.

exercises.explanation: 个 is the general measure word.
exercises.promptTranslation: I have two older sisters.

exercises.explanation: 那位 is the respectful “that person”.
exercises.promptTranslation: That teacher is surnamed Wang.
How many people are there in your family?

exercises.prompt: When do you use 多少 instead of 几?
options: When the number could be larger than ten

lessons.title: 52. Either-or questions: 有没有, 是不是
lessons.subtitle: 你有没有兄弟姐妹？ 这是不是你哥哥？

explanations.title: Verb + not + verb
explanations.body: Besides 吗, there is another yes/no question: put the verb or adjective and its negative side by side. 你有兄弟姐妹吗？ becomes 你有没有兄弟姐妹？ and 这是你哥哥吗？ becomes 这是不是你哥哥？ It is like “Do you have siblings or not?” and can sound a little more direct than 吗. The 不 in the middle is unstressed, in the neutral tone, and with 有 the negative is 没有.

rows: Do you have an older sister (or not)?
zhè shì bu shì nǐ gēge
Is this your older brother (or not)?
Do you look at it (or not)?

explanations.title: Answering
explanations.body: You answer exactly as you would a 吗 question: repeat the verb, or say 不 plus the verb. An answer with 有 or 是 does not repeat the question; it answers it.

examples.text: 你有没有姐姐？ 有，我有两个姐姐。
examples.translation: nǐ yǒu méi yǒu jiějie? yǒu, wǒ yǒu liǎng gè jiějie — Do you have older sisters? Yes, I have two.

examples.text: 这是不是你哥哥？ 不是，这是我弟弟。
examples.translation: zhè shì bu shì nǐ gēge? búshì, zhè shì wǒ dìdi — Is this your older brother? No, it is my younger brother.

examples.text: 那位是不是老师？ 不是，他是我们的班长。
examples.translation: nà wèi shì bu shì lǎoshī? búshì, tā shì wǒmen de bānzhǎng — Is that person a teacher? No, he is our class leader.

exercises.explanation: With 有 the negative is 没有: 有没有.

exercises.explanation: 是不是 goes where 是 was.

lessons.title: 53. Children and grandchildren
lessons.subtitle: 孩子, 儿子, 女儿, 孙子, 外孙女

explanations.title: Your children and theirs
explanations.body: 孩子 is a child or children. 儿子 is a son and 女儿 a daughter. For grandchildren, Chinese separates your son's children from your daughter's: your son's are 孙子 (grandson) and 孙女 (granddaughter), and your daughter's are 外孙 and 外孙女, where 外 means “outside”. 女儿 is written nǚ'ér, with an apostrophe because the second syllable begins with a vowel.

explanations.title: Talking to an older person
explanations.body: 大爷 (and the warmer 老大爷) is a respectful way to speak to an older man. 身体 is the body or your health, 真 means “really”, and 可爱 means cute. Complimenting someone's health is a polite thing to do.

examples.text: 大爷，您身体真好！
examples.translation: dàye, nín shēntǐ zhēn hǎo — Sir, your health is really good!

examples.text: 您有几个孩子？ 两个，一个儿子，一个女儿。
examples.translation: nín yǒu jǐ gè háizi? liǎng gè, yí gè érzi, yí gè nǚ'ér — How many children do you have? Two, a son and a daughter.

examples.text: 你看，这是我孙子，这是我外孙女。
examples.translation: nǐ kàn, zhè shì wǒ sūnzi, zhè shì wǒ wàisūnnǚ — Look, this is my grandson and this is my granddaughter (my daughter's daughter).

examples.text: 你的孩子真可爱！
examples.translation: nǐ de háizi zhēn kě'ài — Your child is really cute!

lessons.title: 54. Jobs
lessons.subtitle: 做什么工作？ 医生, 工程师, 老师, 教官

explanations.title: What do you do?
explanations.body: To ask someone's job, say 做什么工作？, literally “do what work?”. 做 means to do and 工作 means work or a job. To answer, use 是 and the job: 我是医生. 教官 is an instructor, especially in a military school. 家庭主妇 is a homemaker. A 大学生 is a college student and a 中学生 is a middle-school student.

explanations.title: Asking and answering
explanations.body: Asking about a relative uses the same pattern.

examples.text: 你父亲做什么工作？
examples.translation: nǐ fùqīn zuò shénme gōngzuò — What does your father do?

examples.text: 他是军校教官。
examples.translation: tā shì jūnxiào jiàoguān — He is an instructor at a military school.

examples.translation: nǐ mǔqīn ne? tā shì jiātíng zhǔfù — And your mother? She is a homemaker.

examples.translation: wǒ dàgē shì yīshēng, èrgē shì gōngchéngshī — My eldest brother is a doctor and my second brother is an engineer.

exercises.explanation: 家庭主妇 (jiātíng zhǔfù) means “a homemaker”.

lessons.title: 55. Places of work and study
lessons.subtitle: 医院, 公司, 学校, 军校, 学院

explanations.title: Where people work and study
explanations.body: 医院 is a hospital and 公司 is a company. 学校 is a school. 军校 is a military school, short for 军事学校. 中学 is a middle or high school, 大学 is a university and 学院 is a college or institute, as in 空军学院, an air force academy. In these words 学 means study and 校 means school.

explanations.title: Who works where
explanations.body: Jobs and places match up in a typical family.

exercises.explanation: 空军学院 (kōngjūn xuéyuàn) means “an air force academy”.

lessons.title: 56. At a place: 在 and 哪儿
lessons.subtitle: 他在医院工作 · 你在哪儿工作？

explanations.title: 在 puts the place before the verb
explanations.body: 在 means “at” or “in”. The place phrase comes before the verb in Chinese, where English puts it after: 他在医院工作 is “he at-hospital works”. The pattern is Subject + 在 + place + verb. 在 is also a verb by itself, “to be at”, as in 老师在家, “the teacher is at home”.

explanations.title: 哪儿 means “where”
explanations.body: 哪儿 asks for a place. It is written nǎ'er in pinyin and said nǎr: the 儿 is a small “r” sound added to the end of the syllable. As always, the question word sits in the place the answer will go.

examples.text: 你在哪儿工作？
examples.translation: nǐ zài nǎ'er gōngzuò — Where do you work?

examples.text: 我在医院工作。

examples.translation: lǎoshī zài nǎ'er? lǎoshī zài jiā — Where is the teacher? The teacher is at home.

exercises.explanation: 在 (zài) means “at, in; to be at”.

lessons.title: 57. Verb + object phrases
lessons.subtitle: 教书, 上课, 说话, 吃饭, 看书

explanations.title: Common verb + object pairs
explanations.body: Many everyday actions in Chinese are a verb with its own object, and the pair often translates into a single English verb. 教书 is “teach books” and means to teach. 吃饭 is “eat rice” and means to eat. 说话 is “speak words”, to talk. 上课 means to have a class, and 上大学 is to go to college. With an object in the pair you can still add a more specific object: 教英文, 说中文.

rows: to read, to look at a book

explanations.title: Combining with 在
explanations.body: Put 在 and a place before the whole phrase.

units.title: 第三课 Age, numbers and sounds

lessons.title: 59. Asking and telling age
lessons.subtitle: 你今年多大？ 您多大年纪了？ 你几岁了？

explanations.title: Three ways to ask, by age
explanations.body: Chinese has a different way of asking depending on who you ask. For a child under about ten, ask 你几岁了？, using 几 because the answer is a small number. For anyone older than that, an adult or a classmate, ask 你今年多大？. For an older person, about fifty or above, ask more respectfully: 您今年多大年纪了？ 今年 is “this year”, 多大 literally “how big”, and 年纪 and 岁数 both mean age.

rows: How old are you? (to a child)
How old are you? (to an adult or peer)
nín jīnnián duō dà niánjì le
How old are you? (to an older person)

explanations.title: Telling your age
explanations.body: Say 我今年 and the number. 岁 comes straight after the number and means “years old”. With a two-digit number you may leave 岁 out: 我今年二十五. With a single digit you keep it: 我今年八岁.

examples.text: 小朋友，你几岁了？ 我六岁。
examples.translation: xiǎopéngyou, nǐ jǐ suì le? wǒ liù suì — Little one, how old are you? I am six.

examples.text: 你今年多大？ 我今年二十五。
examples.translation: nǐ jīnnián duō dà? wǒ jīnnián èrshíwǔ — How old are you? I am twenty-five.

examples.text: 您今年多大年纪了？ 我今年六十九了。
examples.translation: nín jīnnián duō dà niánjì le? wǒ jīnnián liùshíjiǔ le — How old are you? I am sixty-nine.

examples.text: 我孙子八岁，外孙女五岁。
examples.translation: wǒ sūnzi bā suì, wàisūnnǚ wǔ suì — My grandson is eight, and my granddaughter is five.

lessons.title: 60. The particles 了 and 吧
lessons.subtitle: 您多大年纪了？ 你是中国人吧？

explanations.title: 了 softens a sentence
explanations.body: Put 了 on the end of an age question or answer and it sounds softer and more polite: 你今年多大了？ is gentler than 你今年多大？ The meaning is the same in English. 了 has other jobs too, such as showing that something has changed or finished, and you will meet them later. For now it softens questions and answers about age.

examples.text: 您多大年纪了？
examples.translation: nín duō dà niánjì le — How old are you? (soft and polite)

examples.text: 我今年二十五了。
examples.translation: wǒ jīnnián èrshíwǔ le — I am twenty-five.

examples.text: 他们几岁了？ 他们八岁了。
examples.translation: tāmen jǐ suì le? tāmen bā suì le — How old are they? They are eight.

explanations.title: 吧 asks for confirmation
explanations.body: 吧 on the end of a statement turns it into a question that expects the answer “yes”: you think you know, and you want to check. 你是中国人吧？ is “You are Chinese, right?” A positive answer is often 对. Compare it with 吗, which is a plain open question.

rows: He is your older brother, right?
Your instructor is a major, right?

explanations.title: A quick example
explanations.body: Answering a 吧 question is easy: confirm with 对 or correct it.

examples.text: 你妈妈是韩国人吧？ 对，我妈妈是韩国人。
examples.translation: nǐ māma shì Hánguó rén ba? duì, wǒ māma shì Hánguó rén — Your mother is Korean, right? Yes, she is.

examples.text: 他们都有孩子了吧？ 有。

lessons.title: 61. Round numbers and 多
lessons.subtitle: 四十多岁 · 一百 · 两千 · 一万

explanations.title: Hundreds, thousands and ten thousands
explanations.body: 百, 千 and 万 are 100, 1,000 and 10,000. They work like 十: 三百 is 300, 四千 is 4,000, 五万 is 50,000. For 100, 1,000 and 10,000 you say the 一 first: 一百, 一千, 一万. For 200, 2,000 and 20,000 you normally use 两: 两百, 两千, 两万. The 一 in 一百 and 一千 is said yì, and in 一万 it is said yí.

explanations.title: “More than…”: 多 after the number
explanations.body: 多 after a round number means “and a bit more”, so 四十多 is “forty-odd”, more than forty. It goes after the 十, 百, 千 or 万, and then comes the measure word and the noun: 三十多个学生 is “more than thirty students”. It is a rough number, so it fits ages, crowds and sizes.

examples.text: 我们学校有一千多个学生。

lessons.title: 62. Military numbers
lessons.subtitle: 洞 幺 两 三 四 五 六 拐 八 勾

explanations.title: Why there are two sets of digits
explanations.body: Many numbers sound alike, especially over a radio or a bad phone line: yī and qī, sì and shí. So the Chinese military uses its own spoken digits. Four of them are different words entirely (0 is 洞, 1 is 幺, 7 is 拐, 9 is 勾), 2 is said 两 instead of 二, and 5 is said wù instead of wǔ. 3, 4, 6 and 8 are the same as usual. Taiwan's armed forces use the same system.

explanations.title: Reading numbers on the radio
explanations.body: Military digits are said one at a time, whatever the size of the number. So 1000 is not “one thousand” but “yāo dòng dòng dòng”, and 007 is “dòng dòng guǎi”. Here is how some numbers sound.

examples.text: 幺两三
examples.translation: yāo liǎng sān — 1 2 3

examples.text: 三四六
examples.translation: sān sì liù — 3 4 6 (the same as civilian digits)

examples.text: 拐八勾洞
examples.translation: guǎi bā gōu dòng — 7 8 9 0

examples.text: 幺洞洞洞
examples.translation: yāo dòng dòng dòng — 1000 (one, zero, zero, zero)

examples.text: 洞洞拐
examples.translation: dòng dòng guǎi — 007

lessons.title: 63. Lucky numbers and number scripts
lessons.subtitle: 6, 8, 9 and 4 · 520 · 壹 贰 叁

explanations.title: Numbers that sound like other words
explanations.body: Chinese is full of word play, and numbers join in because many words share a sound. 8 (bā) is liked because it rhymes with 发 (fā), “get rich”. 6 (liù) sounds like 溜, “smooth”, and 禄, “good fortune”. 9 (jiǔ) sounds like 久, “lasting a long time”. 4 (sì) sounds like 死 (sǐ), “to die”, so some buildings skip floor 4 and some people avoid it.

explanations.title: Number messages
explanations.body: Strings of digits are used as messages. 520, wǔ èr líng, sounds like 我爱你, “I love you”, and May 20 is treated as a day for gifts. 518 sounds like 我要发, “I will get rich”, and 168 like 一路发, “prosperity all the way”.

explanations.title: Three ways to write numbers
explanations.body: Arabic digits (阿拉伯数字) are used for calculation, signs and phone numbers. Chinese-character numbers (汉字数字), such as 一二三, are used in text. A third set, the formal capital numbers (大写数字), uses more complicated characters that are hard to alter, so they are used on cheques and in accounting to prevent fraud. Zero can be written 〇 or 零.

exercises.explanation: 八 bā is close to 发 fā.

九 jiǔ and 久 jiǔ sound the same.

lessons.title: 64. Sound pairs: z/zh, s/sh, j/zh, x/sh, r
lessons.subtitle: 早 · 找 · 三 · 山 · 少校 · 日本

explanations.title: z against zh, s against sh
explanations.body: These pairs differ only in where the tongue is: flat against the teeth for z and s, curled back for zh and sh.

explanations.title: j against zh, x against sh, and r
explanations.body: j and x are made with the tongue tip down behind the lower teeth and the middle of the tongue raised, zh and sh with the tip curled back. r is a curled, buzzing sound, like a soft English “r” without rounding the lips too much.

赞 is read zàn and means “to praise”.

lessons.title: 65. The ü syllables: yu, yue, yuan, yun
lessons.subtitle: 鱼 语 月 远 云 运 · 选举 句子 决定

explanations.title: When ü stands alone
explanations.body: A syllable cannot start with a bare ü. The spelling rule is to write y in front and drop the dots: ü becomes yu, üe becomes yue, üan becomes yuan and ün becomes yun. Do not be fooled by the u, since these are all really ü sounds, with rounded lips. Compare yuè (月, a month) with yè (夜, night), and yún (云, a cloud) with yín (银, silver).

tables.title: With y: yu, yue, yuan, yun

explanations.title: After j, q and x
explanations.body: After j, q and x the same ü is also written u, because j, q and x never go with a real u. Say each word with rounded lips.

tables.title: ü after j, q, x and y

lessons.title: 66. Military words: pistols
lessons.subtitle: 手枪 · 左轮手枪 · 自动手枪 · 五四式

explanations.title: Naming pistols
explanations.body: 手 is the hand and 枪 is a firearm, so 手枪 is a pistol, a “hand gun”. Types are named by a word in front. 左轮 means “left wheel”, from the turning cylinder, so 左轮手枪 is a revolver. 自动 means automatic, so 自动手枪 is an automatic pistol. Models are named with a number and 式, which means “type” or “model”: 五四式手枪 is the Type 54 pistol and 五九式手枪 the Type 59. These are names of Chinese service pistols. The table gives the ordinary reading; in military speech the 五 is said wù, as in Lesson 62.

explanations.title: Reading the model numbers
explanations.body: In the military the model name is read with military digits, so 五 is wù. Compare this with 手机, “cell phone”: it also begins with 手, “hand”.

units.title: 第四课 Dates and birthdays

lessons.title: 68. Months and days
lessons.subtitle: 一月 · 十二月 · 三月十四号

explanations.title: Months are numbered
explanations.body: A month is its number plus 月 (yuè), which also means “moon”. January is “month one”, 一月, and December is “month twelve”, 十二月. There are no separate names to learn. In the names of months the 一 stays in the 1st tone (yī), because it is a name and not an amount.

explanations.title: Days of the month
explanations.body: The day is its number plus 号 (hào) in speech and 日 (rì) in writing. The larger unit comes first in Chinese: month, then day. So March 14 is 三月十四号, “March, fourteenth”.

examples.text: 三月十四号
examples.translation: sānyuè shísìhào — March 14

examples.text: 七月四号
examples.translation: qīyuè sìhào — July 4

examples.translation: yīyuè yīhào — January 1

exercises.explanation: 号 is spoken; 日 is written.

lessons.title: 69. Days of the week
lessons.subtitle: 星期一 … 星期天 · 周一

explanations.title: 星期 and a number
explanations.body: The days of the week are just numbered, like the months: 星期 (xīngqī) plus a number. Monday is 星期一 and Saturday is 星期六. Sunday is the one exception: it is 星期天 in speech and 星期日 in writing, never 星期七. A shorter, less formal form uses 周 (zhōu): 周一 is Monday and 周日 is Sunday. To ask which day, put 几 in the number's place: 今天星期几？

explanations.title: Talking about the week
explanations.body: Use 是 for “is” with a day, and you may leave it out: 今天(是)星期四. Put 下 before 星期 or 周 for “next” and 上 for “last”.

examples.text: 今天星期几？ 今天星期四。
examples.translation: jīntiān xīngqījǐ? jīntiān xīngqīsì — What day is it today? It is Thursday.

examples.text: 明天是星期五。

exercises.explanation: 几 stands in for the number after 星期.

lessons.title: 70. Years and counting time
lessons.subtitle: 二零零二年 · 两年 · 三天 · 两个星期

explanations.title: Saying a year
explanations.body: A year is read digit by digit, then 年 (nián): 2002 is 二零零二年, “two zero zero two year”. Zero is 零. In years, 一 stays yī. Just as in months, the word 年 is the last thing you say.

explanations.title: How long? Counting time
explanations.body: To count years or days, say the number and 年 or 天 directly: 三年 is “three years”, 五天 “five days”. Weeks and months need the measure word 个: 两个星期, 三个月. For “two”, use 两 in an amount but 二 in a date or a year: 二月 is February, but 两个月 is two months. Before 年, 一 changes to the 4th tone: 一年 is yì nián, “one year”.

exercises.explanation: Read the digits one by one, then 年.
两 before 年 for an amount; 年 takes no 个.
Weeks need 个: 两个星期.
三月 would be March; 三个月 is three months.

lessons.title: 71. Asking the date
lessons.subtitle: 今天几号？ · 今年是哪一年？ · 明年 · 下个月

explanations.title: Questions about the date
explanations.body: Replace the number with 几 for a month, a day or a day of the week. For a year, use 哪一年, “which year”. You may add 是, but you do not have to: 今天(是)几号？ The larger unit comes first, so a full date runs year, month, day, weekday.

explanations.title: Time words
explanations.body: These words set the time. 今 is “this”, 明 “tomorrow or next”, 昨 and 去 “yesterday or last”.

examples.translation: jīntiān shì sānyuè wǔhào, xīngqīsān — Today is March 5, Wednesday.

exercises.explanation: 下个月 (xià gè yuè) means “next month”.

lessons.title: 72. Birthdays
lessons.subtitle: 生日 · 你的生日是几月几号？ · 真巧！ · 太好了！

explanations.title: Asking about a birthday
explanations.body: 生日 (shēngrì) is a birthday. Ask 你的生日是几月几号？ and answer with the date. To ask the weekday, say 你的生日是星期几？ 过 (guò) means to celebrate or to spend a day, so 过生日 is to celebrate a birthday, and you wish someone 生日快乐, “happy birthday”.

rows: nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ hào
我的生日是五月二十号。
wǒ de shēngrì shì wǔyuè èrshíhào

explanations.title: Little words for a chat
explanations.body: Some small words make a conversation sound natural. 真巧 (zhēn qiǎo) is “what a coincidence”, 太好了 (tài hǎo le) “wonderful”, 对了 (duì le) “by the way”, and 哦 (ò) is a surprised “oh”. 啦 (la) is a lively 了, and 和 (hé) is “and”. 可以 (kěyǐ) means “can” or “may”.

examples.translation: wǒmen de shēngrì dōu shì sānyuè sānhào. zhēn qiǎo — Our birthdays are both March 3. What a coincidence!

examples.text: 今天是我的生日。 生日快乐！

examples.text: 对了，你的生日是星期几？
examples.translation: duìle, nǐ de shēngrì shì xīngqī jǐ — By the way, what day is your birthday?

exercises.explanation: 过生日 (guò shēngrì) means “to celebrate a birthday”.
真巧 (zhēn qiǎo) means “what a coincidence”.

lessons.title: 73. The twelve animals
lessons.subtitle: 属马 · 鼠 牛 虎 兔 龙 蛇 马 羊 猴 鸡 狗 猪

explanations.title: A year for each animal
explanations.body: Chinese years run in a cycle of twelve animals, and you belong to the animal of your birth year. 属 (shǔ) means “to belong to”, so you say 我属马, “I am a horse”. The cycle repeats every twelve years: 2002 is a horse year, 马年, and so are 2014 and 2026. The zodiac year begins at the Spring Festival, so a birthday in early January or February can belong to the animal of the year before.

explanations.title: Asking and answering
explanations.body: Ask 你属什么？ and answer 我属 plus the animal. You can also talk about the year itself: 2020 is 鼠年, a rat year.

examples.text: 你属什么？ 我属马。

examples.text: 今年是鼠年，明年是牛年。
examples.translation: jīnnián shì shǔnián, míngnián shì niúnián — This year is the rat year, next year the ox year.

examples.text: 二零零一年是蛇年，我姐姐属蛇。
examples.translation: èr líng líng yī nián shì shénián, wǒ jiějie shǔ shé — 2001 is a snake year, and my older sister is a snake.

lessons.title: 74. Born in: the 是…的 pattern
lessons.subtitle: 你是哪年出生的？ · 我是在纽约出生的。

explanations.title: Asking about a known event
explanations.body: 出生 (chūshēng) means “to be born”. To ask when or where it happened, Chinese uses the pattern 是 … 的. You use it when both people already know that something happened and you want the details: when, where, how or with whom. 是 goes before the detail, and 的 goes at the end of the sentence. In everyday speech you may drop 是: 他在纽约出生的.

rows: 我是二零零二年出生的。

explanations.title: What the detail can be
explanations.body: The detail sits between 是 and the verb. Questions use 哪一年, 在哪儿 and 什么时候 (shénme shíhou, “when”) in the same place.

examples.text: 你是哪一年出生的？
examples.translation: nǐ shì nǎ yì nián chūshēng de — What year were you born?

examples.text: 我是二零零二年出生的。
examples.translation: wǒ shì èr líng líng èr nián chūshēng de — I was born in 2002.

examples.text: 他是在纽约出生的。
examples.translation: tā shì zài niǔyuē chūshēng de — He was born in New York.

examples.text: 你是什么时候认识你太太的？
examples.translation: nǐ shì shénme shíhou rènshi nǐ tàitai de — When did you meet your wife?

examples.text: 我们是昨天来的。
examples.translation: wǒmen shì zuótiān lái de — We came yesterday.

lessons.title: 75. 是…的: no and questions
lessons.subtitle: 他不是在纽约出生的。 · 他是不是在纽约出生的？

explanations.title: Saying no
explanations.body: To deny the detail, put 不 before 是: 不是 + detail + verb + 的. This time you cannot drop 是. So 他不是在纽约出生的 means “He was not born in New York”; the real place is something else.

rows: 是不是 + detail + verb + 的？
他是不是在纽约出生的？

explanations.title: Both questions mean the same
explanations.body: A yes/no question can end with 吗 or use 是不是 before the detail. 是不是 is a bit more neutral. Answer with 是 or 不是, then add the real detail.

examples.text: 你是在北京出生的吗？ 是，我是在北京出生的。
examples.translation: nǐ shì zài běijīng chūshēng de ma? shì, wǒ shì zài běijīng chūshēng de — Were you born in Beijing? Yes, I was.

examples.text: 你是不是在北京出生的？ 不是，我是在上海出生的。

lessons.title: 76. 就 for emphasis and “soon”
lessons.subtitle: 下星期就是我的生日了 · 她就是南方人

explanations.title: 就 means “exactly”
explanations.body: 就 (jiù) comes before a verb, a place phrase or 是 to stress a fact, like “indeed” or “exactly” in English. Before a noun or an adjective you need 是 too: 就是. 她就是南方人, “She is a southerner, indeed”. 我就住在这儿 is “I live right here”.

rows: My hometown is right in the north of China.

explanations.title: 就 also means “soon”
explanations.body: With a time word, 就 can mean that something comes soon or is close: 下星期就是我的生日了, “my birthday is already next week”. The 了 at the end adds the feeling of “it is almost here”.

lessons.title: 77. Holidays
lessons.subtitle: 春节 · 新年 · 国庆节 · 圣诞节 · 感恩节

explanations.title: Festivals with a fixed date
explanations.body: 节 (jié) is a festival or holiday. Some have the same date every year in the usual calendar: New Year is January 1, Labour Day May 1, American Independence Day July 4, China's National Day October 1 and Christmas December 25. The Spring Festival, 春节, follows the old calendar, so its date moves from late January to mid-February, and Qingming is in early April. Thanksgiving is on the fourth Thursday of November.

explanations.title: Talking about them
explanations.body: Ask 春节是几月几号？ for a date and say what you will do with 过: 过春节 is to celebrate the Spring Festival. 一起 (yìqǐ) means “together”.

lessons.title: 78. The tone changes of 一
lessons.subtitle: yī · yì · yí: 一个 · 一年 · 一点儿

explanations.title: Three tones for one character
explanations.body: The character 一 (“one”) is the 1st tone, yī, when it stands alone, ends a word or is an ordinal: 一, 二, 三; 二十一; 星期一; 一月. Before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone it becomes the 4th tone, yì: 一张照片 (yì zhāng zhàopiàn), 一年 (yì nián), 一点儿 (yìdiǎnr). Before a 4th tone it becomes the 2nd, yí: 一个 (yí gè). The pinyin in this app shows the changed tone, so just read what you see.

rows: alone or at the end: yī

explanations.title: A quick method
explanations.body: Look at the syllable after 一. If it is a 4th tone, say yí. If it is anything else, say yì. If nothing follows, say yī.

units.title: 第四课 Hometowns and places

lessons.title: 80. Being somewhere: 在 and 老家
lessons.subtitle: 他在北京 · 张老师不在 · 你的老家在哪儿？

explanations.title: 在 as a verb
explanations.body: As a verb, 在 (zài) means “to be at” a place. 他在北京 is “He is in Beijing”. With no place word it means “is here” or “is in”, the place being known: 张老师不在, “Teacher Zhang is not in”. Its negative is 不在, and questions are 在吗？ or 在不在？ 老家 (lǎojiā) is your hometown, the place your family comes from, and 现在 (xiànzài) is “now”.

rows: Teacher Zhang is not in today.
Is Teacher Li in the classroom?

explanations.title: Verb 在, or place before a verb?
explanations.body: When 在 comes before another verb, it is not the main verb: it shows where the action happens. 他在北京工作 is “He works in Beijing”; the verb is 工作. When 在 stands by itself, it is the verb “to be at”: 他在北京.

examples.text: 我的老家在四川。

lessons.title: 81. East, south, west, north
lessons.subtitle: 东南西北 · 东部 · 南边 · 南方人

explanations.title: The four directions
explanations.body: The four directions are 东 (dōng, east), 南 (nán, south), 西 (xī, west) and 北 (běi, north). When Chinese names them in a list, the order is 东南西北, east-south-west-north. Two directions together give the corners, and the first one named is the main one: 东南 is the southeast, 西北 the northwest.

explanations.title: Three ways to use them
explanations.body: Add 部 (bù, a part) to name a region: 东部 is the eastern part. Add 边 (biān, side) to say which side of something: 南边 is the south side. Add 方 (fāng, direction) and 人 for people: 南方人 are southerners and 北方人 northerners.

examples.text: 我的老家在美国东部。
examples.translation: wǒ de lǎojiā zài měiguó dōngbù — My hometown is in the eastern United States.

examples.text: 他们住在西部。
examples.translation: tāmen zhù zài xībù — They live in the west.

exercises.prompt: What is the Chinese order of the four directions in a list?

exercises.explanation: 东 + 北, east named first.

lessons.title: 82. Where one place is
lessons.subtitle: 天津在北京的南边 · 在中国的西北部

explanations.title: A is south of B
explanations.body: To place one thing against another, use 在 and 的 with a direction word: A 在 B 的 南边. The part you are locating comes first and the landmark second, with 的 in between. 天津在北京的南边 is “Tianjin is south of Beijing”. To place something inside a larger area, say the area and then the part: 在中国的西北部, “in the northwest of China”.

A 在 B 的 东部

lessons.title: 83. Cities, states and bases
lessons.subtitle: 大城市 · 小城市 · 纽约州 · 军事基地

explanations.title: Big city, small city
explanations.body: 城市 (chéngshì) is a city. Add 大 (big) or 小 (small): 大城市 and 小城市. 州 (zhōu) is a state; the big divisions of China are provinces, 省 (shěng). Add 州 to a state's short name: 纽约州 is New York state, and 德州 and 加州 are Texas and California. A place name takes 的 and 一个 when you describe it: 纽约州的一个小城市, “a small city in New York State”.

explanations.title: Describing a place
explanations.body: Say what kind of place it is with 是 and the size, or place it with 在: 上海是一个大城市. 我父母现在住在西部的一个军事基地 is “My parents now live on a military base in the west”.

lessons.title: 84. Where are you from?
lessons.subtitle: 你是哪儿人？ · 我是北京人 · 我是广东人

explanations.title: 哪儿人
explanations.body: To ask where someone is from, say 你是哪儿人？ and answer with the place plus 人: 我是北京人, “I am from Beijing”, literally “a Beijing person”. It also works with a country (我是美国人) and a region (我是南方人). A polite form is 您是哪儿的人？ and a question about the hometown itself is 你的老家在哪儿？ When you speak about a group, 都 means all of them, and 不都 means “not all”.

explanations.title: Southerners and northerners
explanations.body: If you only know the region, say 南方人 or 北方人. A group can be mixed, and then you say 有 … 也有 …, “there are … and also …”.

lessons.title: 85. Born and grown up
lessons.subtitle: 我是在那儿出生，长大的。 · 长 zhǎng

explanations.title: 长大: to grow up
explanations.body: 长大 (zhǎngdà) means “to grow up”. Here 长 is read zhǎng, “to grow”, and not cháng, “long”. It fits the 是…的 pattern you already know, since you know the person grew up and now give the place: 我是在那儿长大的. You can join two verbs after one place: 我是在四川出生，长大的.

explanations.title: Telling your story
explanations.body: Combine what you know. After a question like 你是在那儿出生的吗？, a full answer repeats the pattern.

lessons.title: 86. Still: 还 and 不…了
lessons.subtitle: 你父母还住在那儿吗？ · 他们不住在那儿了。

explanations.title: 还 means “still”
explanations.body: 还 (hái) before a verb means “still” or “yet”. 她还教我们中文 is “She still teaches us Chinese”. To ask, add 吗: 她还教你们中文吗？ To say it is no longer so, use 不 … 了: 她不教我们中文了, “She no longer teaches us Chinese”. 了 here marks a change.

explanations.title: Where do your parents live?
explanations.body: A natural conversation about the family uses all three forms together.

lessons.title: 87. Which one? 哪 + measure word
lessons.subtitle: 哪位老师 · 哪个州 · 哪国人 · 哪个班

explanations.title: 哪 needs a measure word
explanations.body: 哪 (nǎ) means “which”. In Chinese a noun that follows 哪 needs a measure word in between: 哪位老师, “which teacher”, and never 哪老师. The measure word is the same one you would use to count the noun: 位 for people you respect, 个 for most things, and 国 in 哪国人, “which country's person”.

rows: 哪个同学是你们的班长？
Which student is your class leader?
Which state is your hometown in?

explanations.title: Answering
explanations.body: Answer by naming the thing. 哪 (nǎ, “which”) is a different word from 哪儿 (nǎr, “where”) and from 那 (nà, “that”).

lessons.title: 88. Surprise: the question with no particle
lessons.subtitle: 你是南方人？ · 你没有哥哥？

explanations.title: Rising tone, no particle
explanations.body: A yes/no question usually ends in 吗 or 吧. But when you are surprised, you can take the word order of a statement, add no particle at all, and raise your voice at the end. 你是南方人？ means “You are from the south?!”. You use it when you have just learned something unexpected, and you want it confirmed.

rows: I did not know you were a teacher.

explanations.title: Choosing between the three
explanations.body: 吗 asks openly. 吧 says “I think so, right?”. A question with no particle says “Really? I had not expected that”.

lessons.title: 89. All, not all, none: 都, 不都, 都不
lessons.subtitle: 我们都是 · 我们不都是 · 我们都不是

explanations.title: Three degrees
explanations.body: 都 (dōu) means “all” or “both” and sits after the subject, before the verb. The order of 不 and 都 changes the meaning. 不都 is a partial negative: “not all”, some are and some are not. 都不 is a full negative: “none”, “neither”. So 我们班不都是海军 means some of the class are in the Navy and some are not, while 我们班都不是海军 means nobody in the class is.

rows: 我们不都是中文系的学生。
Not all of us are Chinese majors.
他们都不是韩语系的学生。
None of them are Korean majors.

explanations.title: Pairs of people
explanations.body: With two people, 都 is “both” and 都不 is “neither”.

lessons.title: 90. The -r ending
lessons.subtitle: 花儿 · 这儿 · 哪儿 · 一会儿 · 玩儿

explanations.title: er becomes r
explanations.body: The sound er (ér, 儿, “son”) can be added at the end of a word, and then it shrinks to a retroflex r. It is typical of the Beijing dialect and is spoken by many northerners. In writing, the character 儿 is added, and in pinyin only an r: 花 + 儿 gives 花儿 (huār), “flower”. Curl your tongue back as you finish the syllable. After -i, -n or -ng, those endings fade when you say it, but the pinyin keeps them: 小孩儿 (xiǎoháir), 玩儿 (wánr), 电影儿 (diànyǐngr).

explanations.title: What the r does
explanations.body: The -r can do three jobs. It can make a thing small or dear: 小鸟儿 is a little bird. It can change the meaning of a word: 头 is a head but 头儿 is a boss. It can turn a verb into a noun: 画 is to draw and 画儿 is a picture. Words you will use all the time are 这儿, 那儿 and 哪儿, “here, there, where”.

lessons.title: 91. Ship words
lessons.subtitle: 军舰 · 潜艇 · 驱逐舰 · 航空母舰

explanations.title: 舰 and 艇
explanations.body: Two characters tell you the size of a vessel. 舰 (jiàn) is a large warship and 艇 (tǐng) a small boat or a submarine. Put a word in front to say what the vessel does: 巡洋 means cruising the oceans, 驱逐 is to drive off, 扫雷 is to sweep mines and 补给 is to supply. These are names to recognise; later lessons use them in sentences.

explanations.title: A word to use them
explanations.body: 海军 (hǎijūn) is the Navy. 他是海军 says he is a sailor. For now, point and name the vessels with 这是 and 那是.

lessons.title: 92. Classroom expressions
lessons.subtitle: 现在我们做听力练习 · 请你慢一点儿说

explanations.title: What your teacher says
explanations.body: These are phrases your teacher uses every day. The first tells you to sit: 上课了，请坐好, “Class has started, please sit properly”. Then comes 现在我们做 plus a kind of 练习 (liànxí, “exercise”). Learn the kinds by their parts: 语音 is pronunciation, 听力 listening, 阅读 reading, 会话 conversation, 翻译 translation, 听写 dictation, 写字 writing characters.

explanations.title: Phrases to ask the teacher

lessons.title: 93. The Chinese family
lessons.subtitle: 家人 · 国家 · 四世同堂 · 回老家过春节

explanations.title: Family in Chinese life
explanations.body: The family has been central to Chinese society for thousands of years. 国家 (guójiā) is the word for a nation, and it is made of 国 (country) and 家 (family): a nation is a “national family”. Respect for elders is a core value. The old ideal was 四世同堂 (sìshìtóngtáng): four generations living under one roof. 家人 (jiārén) means the people in your family.

rows: to go back to one's hometown

explanations.title: Spring Festival and small families
explanations.body: Around the Spring Festival, millions of people travel to their hometowns to be with their families. It is the biggest yearly journey of people in the world. From 1979 until 2016, a policy limited most couples to one child (独生子女政策), so many children grew up as an only child, a 独生子女 (dúshēng zǐnǚ). Today the typical urban family is small, and more grandparents help raise children, while 养老院 (yǎnglǎoyuàn), homes for older people, are a newer trend.

units.title: 第五课 Cities and population

lessons.title: 95. Ten thousand and a hundred million
lessons.subtitle: 万 · 亿 · 十多万 · 三百多万 · 九百多亿

explanations.title: Chinese counts in ten-thousands
explanations.body: English counts in thousands, then millions. Chinese counts in 万 (wàn, 10,000) and 亿 (yì, 100,000,000). So 100,000 is “ten ten-thousands”, 十万, and a million is “a hundred ten-thousands”, 一百万. A hundred million is 一亿. The number is built the way you build any other: 三百万 is 3,000,000, and 五千万 is 50,000,000. Before 万 and 亿 the 一 changes to yí: 一万, 一亿.

explanations.title: 多 after the round number
explanations.body: To say “more than” a big number, put 多 after the whole round number and before 万 or 亿. 三百多万 is “over three million” and 十多万 is “over 100,000”. This is different from small numbers, where 多 comes last (二十多 for “twenty-odd”).

examples.text: 我的老家有三百多万人口。

examples.text: 这个公司有八千多万个用户。
examples.translation: zhè gè gōngsī yǒu bāqiānduōwàn gè yònghù — This company has more than 80 million users.

lessons.title: 96. Zeros inside a number, and 二 against 两
lessons.subtitle: 一百零五 · 三万零五百 · 两千二百 · 十二万

explanations.title: Say 零 for a gap
explanations.body: When a number has a gap of one or more zeros inside it, you say 零 (líng) once for the whole gap: 105 is 一百零五, 2,008 is 两千零八, 30,500 is 三万零五百. At the end of a round number you do not say 零: 一百 is 100 and 一百二 is shorthand for 120. Nothing is said for the gap when the next digit is just one place down, so 1,100 is 一千一百.

explanations.title: 两 or 二?
explanations.body: As the first digit of 百, 千, 万 or 亿, say 两: 两百, 两千, 两万, 两亿. In the tens and ones places, and in dates and digit strings, say 二: 十二, 二十, 二十二, 二十万 (the “20” is in the tens place of a count of ten-thousands). After a 百 or 千, either may be used, but 两 is the more common: 两千二百.

exercises.explanation: A gap of zero is spoken as 零.

二十 is in the tens place of 万.

lessons.title: 97. Cities and population
lessons.subtitle: 首都 · 人口 · 多少人口 · 只有 · 百分之

explanations.title: Capital, city and people
explanations.body: 人口 (rénkǒu) is population, and you ask about it with 多少: 北京有多少人口？ 首都 (shǒudū) is a capital: 北京是中国的首都. A large number is 多 and a small one is 少 (shǎo, few): 东部人口多, 西部人口少. 只有 (zhǐyǒu) means “has only”, and 很少 means “very few” or “rarely”. 百分之 (bǎifēnzhī) is “percent”: 百分之五十 is 50 percent.

explanations.title: Talking about a place
explanations.body: Put these together to describe a hometown: its size, its people and its place.

examples.text: 北京是中国的首都。
examples.translation: běijīng shì zhōngguó de shǒudū — Beijing is the capital of China.

examples.text: 北京有多少人口？ 北京有两千多万人口。
examples.translation: běijīng yǒu duōshǎo rénkǒu? běijīng yǒu liǎngqiān duōwàn rénkǒu — What is the population of Beijing? More than 20 million.

examples.text: 我的老家是一个小城市，只有十几万人。
examples.translation: wǒ de lǎojiā shì yí gè xiǎo chéngshì, zhǐ yǒu shíjǐwàn rén — My hometown is a small city with only a few hundred thousand people.

examples.text: 中国东部人口多，西部人口少。
examples.translation: zhōngguó dōngbù rénkǒu duō, xībù rénkǒu shǎo — The east of China has many people and the west has few.

examples.text: 我们班有百分之五十的同学是东部人。

exercises.explanation: 多少 (duōshǎo) means “how many, how much”.

lessons.title: 98. The most: 最
lessons.subtitle: 最大 · 最小 · 最多 · 最好 · 最高 · 最低

explanations.title: 最 before an adjective
explanations.body: 最 (zuì) means “the most” and goes before an adjective: 最大 is “biggest”, 最小 “smallest”, 最多 “most”, 最好 “best”, 最高 “highest” and 最低 “lowest”. To use it before a noun, add 的: 最大的城市 is “the biggest city”. The same word works in questions: 谁的中文最好？ asks whose Chinese is best.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Notice how 最 sits right before the adjective, and 的 links the adjective to the noun.

examples.text: 我是我们家最小的孩子。
examples.translation: wǒ shì wǒmen jiā zuì xiǎo de háizi — I am the youngest child in our family.

examples.text: 在我们班，李明的中文最好。
examples.translation: zài wǒmen bān, lǐ míng de zhōngwén zuì hǎo — In our class, Li Ming’s Chinese is the best.

examples.text: 这是我们学校最大的教室。
examples.translation: zhè shì wǒmen xuéxiào zuì dà de jiàoshì — This is the biggest classroom in our school.

examples.text: 在你家，谁的年龄最大？
examples.translation: zài nǐ jiā, shéi de niánlíng zuì dà — In your family, who is the oldest?

exercises.explanation: 最大 is read zuì dà.

lessons.title: 99. Choosing: 还是
lessons.subtitle: 你是南方人还是北方人？ · 东部人口多还是西部人口多？

explanations.title: A or B?
explanations.body: 还是 (háishi) asks the listener to choose between two options, like “or” in a question: Option A 还是 Option B? 你爸爸是北方人还是南方人？ is “Is your father a northerner or a southerner?”. You answer by naming one: 他是南方人. 还是 belongs to questions; a plain statement with “or” uses another word later.

rows: 你爸爸是北方人还是南方人？
Is your father a northerner or a southerner?
东部人口多还是西部人口多？
Does the east or the west have more people?
你的老家在纽约还是在华盛顿？
Is your hometown in New York or Washington?
你姐姐在中学教书还是在大学教书？
Does your sister teach at a middle school or a university?

explanations.title: How to answer
explanations.body: There is no yes or no. Pick one option and say it as a whole short sentence, or just give the option.

examples.text: 你是学生还是老师？ 我是学生。
examples.translation: nǐ shì xuésheng háishi lǎoshī? wǒ shì xuésheng — Are you a student or a teacher? I am a student.

lessons.title: 100. The third tone
lessons.subtitle: 老家 · 老人 · 老师 · 老百姓 · 领子

explanations.title: Third tone before every tone
explanations.body: The third tone dips and rises (ǎ), but when something follows, you only say the dip. In 老家 (lǎojiā), 老人 (lǎorén), 老式 (lǎoshì) the 老 is a low tone that stays down. The big exception: two third tones in a row. The first one becomes a second tone, a rising one: 老手 is written lǎoshǒu but said láoshǒu. The pinyin in the app is spelled with the underlying tone, so you apply the change as you read.

explanations.title: 老 is not always “old”, and 子 is a marker
explanations.body: Used as a prefix, 老 often has no “old” in it: 老师 is a teacher, 老乡 is someone from your home town, 老鹰 is an eagle and 老百姓 means ordinary people. The suffix 子 has no meaning of its own: it marks a noun, and is always in the neutral tone.

exercises.prompt: How is 老 said in 老手?
exercises.explanation: Two third tones in a row: the first rises.

exercises.prompt: How is 老手 really said?
What tone does 子 have in 领子?
exercises.explanation: The suffix 子 is always neutral.

exercises.prompt: What does the suffix 子 mean?

options: No: in 老师 it is just a prefix

lessons.title: 101. Military words: tanks
lessons.subtitle: 坦克 · 装甲车 · 装甲部队 · 轻坦克 · 重坦克

explanations.title: Tanks and armoured vehicles
explanations.body: 坦克 (tǎnkè) is a tank, a word borrowed from English. 装甲 (zhuāngjiǎ) is armour, so 装甲车 is an armoured vehicle. 部队 (bùduì) is a military unit, and so 坦克部队 is a tank unit and 装甲部队 an armoured unit. A word in front says what kind of tank: 轻 (qīng) is light, 重 (zhòng) is heavy, and 两栖 (liǎngqī) is amphibious, “living in two places”.

explanations.title: Using the words
explanations.body: These are names to recognise. Use 这是 and 那是 to point to something, and 他在 plus a unit to say where someone serves.

examples.text: 这是坦克。
examples.translation: zhè shì tǎnkè — This is a tank.

examples.text: 那是装甲车。
examples.translation: nà shì zhuāngjiǎchē — That is an armoured vehicle.

examples.text: 他在坦克部队工作。
examples.translation: tā zài tǎnkè bùduì gōngzuò — He serves in a tank unit.

exercises.explanation: 坦克部队 (tǎnkè bùduì) means “a tank unit”.

exercises.prompt: What does 装甲部队 mean?
exercises.explanation: 装甲部队 (zhuāngjiǎ bùduì) means “an armoured unit”.
轻坦克 (qīng tǎnkè) means “a light tank”.
重坦克 (zhòng tǎnkè) means “a heavy tank”.

exercises.prompt: What does 两栖坦克 mean?
exercises.explanation: 两栖坦克 (liǎngqī tǎnkè) means “an amphibious tank”.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 坦克?
How do you read 装甲车?

units.title: 第五课 Seasons and weather

lessons.title: 103. The four seasons
lessons.subtitle: 春天 · 夏天 · 秋天 · 冬天 · 季节

explanations.title: Spring, summer, autumn, winter
explanations.body: The four seasons are 春天 (chūntiān), 夏天 (xiàtiān), 秋天 (qiūtiān) and 冬天 (dōngtiān), and a season is a 季节 (jìjié). They always come in this order, and 天 (day, sky) is part of each name. A year has four seasons: 一年有四个季节. To ask what someone likes, use 喜欢 (xǐhuan): 你喜欢哪个季节？

explanations.title: Using the seasons
explanations.body: Season words work like time words: put them at the front of the sentence, or after the subject.

examples.text: 一年有四个季节。
examples.translation: yì nián yǒu sì gè jìjié — A year has four seasons.

examples.text: 春天、夏天、秋天和冬天。
examples.translation: chūntiān, xiàtiān, qiūtiān hé dōngtiān — Spring, summer, autumn and winter.

examples.text: 我喜欢春天。
examples.translation: wǒ xǐhuan chūntiān — I like spring.

examples.text: 你喜欢哪个季节？ 我喜欢秋天。
examples.translation: nǐ xǐhuan nǎ gè jìjié? wǒ xǐhuan qiūtiān — Which season do you like? I like autumn.

lessons.title: 104. Weather words
lessons.subtitle: 天气 · 热 · 冷 · 闷热 · 舒服 · 大风 · 大雪

explanations.title: How is the weather?
explanations.body: 天气 (tiānqì) is weather. The basic describing words are 热 (rè, hot) and 冷 (lěng, cold), and 闷热 (mēnrè) is hot and stuffy. 舒服 (shūfu) means comfortable, and in weather talk it is a gentle “nice”. A strong wind is 大风 (dàfēng) and heavy snow 大雪 (dàxuě); 大 here means “strong, heavy”. To say it is a weather: 下雨 (xià yǔ, rain falls), 下雪 (xià xuě, snow falls) and 刮风 (guā fēng, wind blows). 非常 (fēicháng) means “very”, a stronger 很.

explanations.title: Describing a day
explanations.body: Use 天气 as the subject and an adjective after 很 or 非常.

examples.text: 今天天气很冷。
examples.translation: jīntiān tiānqì hěn lěng — The weather is cold today.

examples.text: 夏天非常热，有时候很闷热。
examples.translation: xiàtiān fēicháng rè, yǒu shíhou hěn mēnrè — Summer is very hot, and sometimes hot and stuffy.

examples.text: 秋天的天气很舒服。
examples.translation: qiūtiān de tiānqì hěn shūfu — The weather in autumn is very comfortable.

examples.text: 明天下大雪。
examples.translation: míngtiān xià dà xuě — Tomorrow there will be heavy snow.

exercises.explanation: 刮风 (guā fēng) means “the wind blows”.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 天气?
How do you read 非常?
What does 今天天气很冷 say?
options: Today is a cold day off.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “The wind blows”?

lessons.title: 105. How often it happens
lessons.subtitle: 有时候 · 常常 · 很少 · 下大雨 · 刮大风

explanations.title: Sometimes, often, rarely
explanations.body: 有时候 (yǒushíhou) is “sometimes” and 常常 (chángcháng) is “often”; both go before the verb. 很少 (hěn shǎo) is “rarely”. These time words may start the sentence or follow the subject, but they always come before the verb: 冬天常常下雪.

explanations.title: There and here
explanations.body: 那儿 (nàr) is “there” and 这儿 (zhèr) is “here”. They end in the r sound, which is written 儿 and said as a light r on the previous syllable. Use them for a place: 那儿的冬天很冷 is “Winter there is cold”.

examples.text: 我的老家冬天常常下大雪。
examples.translation: wǒ de lǎojiā dōngtiān chángcháng xià dà xuě — In my hometown it often snows heavily in winter.

examples.text: 那儿夏天有时候很闷热。
examples.translation: nàr xiàtiān yǒushíhou hěn mēnrè — There, summer is sometimes hot and stuffy.

examples.text: 这儿的春天很少刮大风。
examples.translation: zhèr de chūntiān hěn shǎo guā dà fēng — Here it rarely blows hard in spring.

examples.text: 你们那儿夏天热不热？
examples.translation: nǐmen nàr xiàtiān rè bu rè — Is it hot in summer where you are?

exercises.explanation: 下大雨 (xià dà yǔ) means “heavy rain falls”.
Frequency words go before the verb.

exercises.prompt: What does 冬天常常下雪 mean?
What does 这儿的春天很少刮大风 say?
options: Here it rarely blows hard in spring.
exercises.explanation: 很少 is rarely; 这儿 is here.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “sometimes it rains”?
exercises.explanation: 有时候 goes before the verb.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask “Is it hot there in summer?”

lessons.title: 106. Which, how and why
lessons.subtitle: 哪个 · 怎么样 · 为什么

explanations.title: Three question words
explanations.body: 哪个 (nǎge) is “which”: 你喜欢哪个季节？ 怎么样 (zěnmeyàng) is “how about it?”: 北京的天气怎么样？ 为什么 (wèishénme) is “why” and sits before the verb: 你为什么喜欢夏天？ These words stay where the answer would go, and you do not add 吗.

rows: How is the weather in Beijing?
How are winters in your hometown?

explanations.title: Question and answer
explanations.body: Answer 哪个 with the thing, 怎么样 with a description, and 为什么 with 因为 (because).

examples.text: 你喜欢哪个季节？ 我喜欢秋天。
examples.translation: nǐ xǐhuan nǎ gè jìjié? wǒ xǐhuan qiūtiān — Which season do you like? I like autumn.

examples.text: 你为什么喜欢秋天？ 因为秋天很舒服。

lessons.title: 107. Liking most and liking least
lessons.subtitle: 最喜欢 · 最不喜欢 · 不太喜欢

explanations.title: 最喜欢 and 最不喜欢
explanations.body: Put 最 before 喜欢 to say “like best”: 我最喜欢春天. To say “like least”, put 不 between: 最不喜欢. Notice that 最 stays first and 不 sits right before the verb. 不太喜欢 is milder: “do not like very much”.

rows: I do not like summer very much.
Which season do you like best?

explanations.title: Giving a reason
explanations.body: After the choice, add 因为 and a short reason (more in the next lessons).

examples.text: 我最喜欢秋天，因为秋天很舒服。
examples.translation: wǒ zuì xǐhuan qiūtiān, yīnwèi qiūtiān hěn shūfu — I like autumn best because it is comfortable.

examples.text: 我最不喜欢夏天，因为夏天很闷热。
examples.translation: wǒ zuì bù xǐhuan xiàtiān, yīnwèi xiàtiān hěn mēnrè — I like summer least because it is hot and stuffy.

examples.text: 我不太喜欢冬天。
examples.translation: wǒ bú tài xǐhuan dōngtiān — I do not like winter very much.

exercises.prompt: What does 最不喜欢 mean?
exercises.explanation: 最不喜欢 (zuì bù xǐhuan) means “like least”.

exercises.prompt: What does 我最喜欢春天 say?
options: I like spring more than summer.

exercises.prompt: What does 我最不喜欢冬天 say?
options: I do not like winter very much.
exercises.explanation: 最不喜欢 is like least.

options: I do not like summer very much.

I do not like summer very much.

lessons.title: 108. Because … so …
lessons.subtitle: 因为 … 所以 … · 因为冬天下大雪，所以可以滑雪

explanations.title: Reason and result
explanations.body: 因为 (yīnwèi) is “because” and 所以 (suǒyǐ) is “so”. In Chinese they usually come as a pair: 因为 reason, 所以 result. Unlike English, you may say both, and you may drop either one: 因为冬天很冷，所以我不喜欢冬天. Each clause has its own subject, and 所以 starts the result.

rows: 因为冬天很冷，所以我不喜欢冬天。
Because winter is cold, I do not like it.
因为这儿很少下雪，所以不能滑雪。
Because it rarely snows here, we cannot ski.
因为夏天很热，所以我喜欢游泳。
Because summer is hot, I like to swim.

explanations.title: New words
explanations.body: 游泳 (yóuyǒng) is to swim and 滑雪 (huáxuě) is to ski. Both are verbs, and 滑雪 is a verb with its object inside, so it cannot take another object.

examples.text: 因为夏天很热，所以我常常游泳。
examples.translation: yīnwèi xiàtiān hěn rè, suǒyǐ wǒ chángcháng yóuyǒng — Because summer is hot, I often swim.

examples.text: 因为我老家冬天下大雪，所以我们可以滑雪。
examples.translation: yīnwèi wǒ lǎojiā dōngtiān xià dà xuě, suǒyǐ wǒmen kěyǐ huáxuě — Because it snows heavily in my hometown in winter, we can ski.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 所以?
How do you read 游泳?

options: 因为冬天很冷，所以我不喜欢冬天。
因为冬天很冷，因为我不喜欢冬天。
所以冬天很冷，所以我不喜欢冬天。
所以冬天很冷，因为我不喜欢冬天。
exercises.explanation: 因为 reason, 所以 result.

exercises.prompt: What does 因为这儿很少下雪，所以不能滑雪 say?
options: Because we cannot ski, it rarely snows.
It snows often, so we ski.
Because it rarely snows here, we cannot ski.
It rarely snows because we ski.

exercises.prompt: Can you drop 因为 and keep 所以?
因为今天很冷，___我不去游泳。
exercises.promptTranslation: Because it is cold today, I am not going to swim.

exercises.prompt: ___为夏天很热，所以我喜欢游泳。
exercises.promptTranslation: Because summer is hot, I like to swim.

exercises.prompt: 因为冬天下大雪，所以我们可以___雪。
exercises.promptTranslation: Because it snows in winter, we can ski.

exercises.prompt: 因为夏天很热，所以我常常游___。
exercises.promptTranslation: Because summer is hot, I often swim.

lessons.title: 109. Neither … nor …
lessons.subtitle: 不冷也不热 · 不大也不小 · 不多也不少

explanations.title: 不 … 也不 …
explanations.body: To say something is neither one thing nor another, use 不 + A, 也不 + B: 不冷也不热 is “neither cold nor hot”, so “just right”. The two parts are opposites, and 也 means “also”: “not cold, also not hot”. The pattern fits adjectives (不大也不小) and verbs (不吃也不喝).

explanations.title: In a sentence
explanations.body: The whole phrase works as a description: 秋天不冷也不热. It does not need 很.

examples.text: 我老家的春天不冷也不热。
examples.translation: wǒ lǎojiā de chūntiān bù lěng yě bú rè — Spring in my hometown is neither cold nor hot.

examples.text: 那个城市不大也不小。
examples.translation: nà gè chéngshì bú dà yě bù xiǎo — That city is neither big nor small.

examples.text: 我们班的人不多也不少。
examples.translation: wǒmen bān de rén bù duō yě bù shǎo — The number of people in our class is neither many nor few.

exercises.prompt: What does 不冷也不热 mean?
exercises.explanation: 不冷也不热 (bù lěng yě bú rè) means “neither cold nor hot”.

exercises.prompt: What does 不大也不小 mean?
exercises.explanation: 不大也不小 (bú dà yě bù xiǎo) means “neither big nor small”.

exercises.prompt: What does 不多也不少 mean?
exercises.explanation: 不多也不少 (bù duō yě bù shǎo) means “neither many nor few”.

exercises.prompt: What does 秋天不冷也不热 say?
options: Autumn is both cold and hot.
Autumn is neither cold nor hot.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “neither big nor small”?
How do you say “neither cold nor hot”?
Which sentence means “The city is neither big nor small”?
我老家的春天不冷___不热。
exercises.promptTranslation: Spring in my hometown is neither cold nor hot.
That city is neither big nor small.
The number of people in our class is neither many nor few.
Autumn is neither cold nor hot.

lessons.title: 110. Can and cannot: 可以 and 不能
lessons.subtitle: 可以滑雪 · 不能滑雪 · 可以游泳吗？

explanations.title: Allowed or possible
explanations.body: 可以 (kěyǐ) is “can” in the sense of “it is possible or allowed”: 夏天可以游泳. The opposite is 不能 (bù néng), “cannot”: 冬天不能游泳. Both go before the verb. A question is 可以……吗？, and the short answer is 可以 or 不可以, though 不能 is also very common.

rows: Yes, it snows heavily in winter.

explanations.title: With 因为 … 所以 …
explanations.body: Reasons and permission go well together.

examples.text: 因为这儿很少下雪，所以不能滑雪。
examples.translation: yīnwèi zhèr hěn shǎo xià xuě, suǒyǐ bù néng huáxuě — Because it rarely snows here, we cannot ski.

examples.text: 因为我老家冬天下大雪，所以可以滑雪。
examples.translation: yīnwèi wǒ lǎojiā dōngtiān xià dà xuě, suǒyǐ kěyǐ huáxuě — Because it snows heavily in winter in my hometown, we can ski.

examples.text: 你们那儿夏天可以游泳吗？
examples.translation: nǐmen nàr xiàtiān kěyǐ yóuyǒng ma — Can you swim there in summer?

exercises.prompt: How do you read 可以?
What does 夏天可以游泳 say?
options: In summer we like to swim.

exercises.prompt: What does 冬天不能游泳 say?
options: In winter we do not like swimming.

exercises.prompt: Where do 可以 and 不能 go?
How do you ask “Can we ski here?”
Complete: 因为这儿很少下雪，所以___滑雪。
Complete: 因为冬天下大雪，所以___滑雪。

exercises.promptTranslation: In summer we can swim.
In winter we cannot swim.
Can we ski here?

exercises.prompt: 因为这儿很少下雪，所以不___滑雪。
exercises.promptTranslation: Because it rarely snows here, we cannot ski.

lessons.title: 111. Temperature and climate
lessons.subtitle: 温度 · 气温 · 度 · 零下 · 摄氏 · 华氏 · 气候

explanations.title: Degrees
explanations.body: 温度 (wēndù) and 气温 (qìwēn, air temperature) are “temperature”. 度 (dù) is “degree”: 二十度 is 20 degrees. Below zero is 零下 (língxià): 零下五度 is “minus 5”. Two scales: 摄氏 (shèshì) is Celsius and 华氏 (huáshì) is Fahrenheit. 气候 (qìhòu) is climate, the weather over many years, and 天气 is the weather of a day.

explanations.title: Fahrenheit to Celsius
explanations.body: Water freezes at 0 °C, which is 32 °F, and boils at 100 °C, which is 212 °F. To change Fahrenheit into Celsius, subtract 32, then multiply by 5 and divide by 9. So 68 °F is 68 − 32 = 36, times 5 is 180, divided by 9 is 20 °C. The pairs to remember: 50 °F is 10 °C, 68 °F is 20 °C, 86 °F is 30 °C and 104 °F is 40 °C.

examples.text: 今天的气温是二十度。
examples.translation: jīntiān de qìwēn shì èrshí dù — Today’s temperature is 20 degrees.

examples.text: 冬天的气温有时候是零下十度。
examples.translation: dōngtiān de qìwēn yǒushíhou shì língxià shí dù — In winter the temperature is sometimes minus 10.

examples.text: 华氏六十八度是摄氏二十度。
examples.translation: huáshì liùshíbā dù shì shèshì èrshí dù — 68 °F is 20 °C.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 气温?
How do you read 零下?
What is the difference between 天气 and 气候?
options: 天气 is the day’s weather; 气候 is long-term

exercises.promptTranslation: Today’s temperature is 20 degrees.

exercises.prompt: 冬天的气温有时候是零___十度。
exercises.promptTranslation: In winter the temperature is sometimes minus 10.

exercises.prompt: 华氏六十八度是摄氏二十___。

lessons.title: 112. The same as: 跟 … 一样
lessons.subtitle: A 跟 B 一样 · 一样冷 · 不一样

explanations.title: A is the same as B
explanations.body: 跟 (gēn) here means “with”, and 一样 (yíyàng) means “same”. A 跟 B 一样 says “A is the same as B”. To say in what way, add an adjective: A 跟 B 一样冷, “A is as cold as B”. For “different”, use 不一样: A 跟 B 不一样. Note that 一 changes to yí before the fourth tone in 一样.

rows: Beijing is the same as Shanghai.
Beijing is as big as Shanghai.
我老家的冬天跟这儿一样冷。
Winters in my hometown are as cold as here.

explanations.title: Same, or not the same
explanations.body: The negative puts 不 before 一样 only: 不一样 (bù yíyàng). The tones are written as they are said: 不 is bù and 一 is yí.

examples.text: 我的老家跟这儿一样热。
examples.translation: wǒ de lǎojiā gēn zhèr yíyàng rè — My hometown is as hot as here.

examples.text: 夏天的天气跟冬天的天气不一样。
examples.translation: xiàtiān de tiānqì gēn dōngtiān de tiānqì bù yíyàng — The weather in summer is different from the weather in winter.

examples.text: 你的手机跟我的手机一样吗？
examples.translation: nǐ de shǒujī gēn wǒ de shǒujī yíyàng ma — Is your phone the same as mine?

exercises.prompt: How do you read 一样?
What does 北京跟上海一样大 say?
options: Beijing and Shanghai are both small.
Beijing is as big as Shanghai.
exercises.explanation: A 跟 B 一样 + adjective.

exercises.prompt: What does 北京跟上海不一样 say?
options: Beijing is the same as Shanghai.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “My hometown is as hot as here”?
options: 我的老家跟这儿热一样。
我的老家一样跟这儿热。
我的老家这儿跟一样热。
我的老家跟这儿一样热。
exercises.explanation: A 跟 B 一样 + adjective.

exercises.prompt: What does 你的手机跟我的手机一样吗？ ask?
options: Is your phone the same as mine?
exercises.explanation: 跟 … 一样 asks about sameness.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “Summer weather is different from winter weather”?
options: 夏天的天气跟冬天的天气不一样。
夏天的天气跟不一样冬天的天气。
夏天的天气跟冬天的天气一样不。
夏天的天气不一样跟冬天的天气。
exercises.explanation: 不一样 after the second part.

exercises.promptTranslation: Beijing is as big as Shanghai.
My hometown is as hot as here.
Summer is different from winter.

exercises.prompt: 夏天的天气跟冬天的天气___一样。
exercises.promptTranslation: The weather in summer is different from winter.

lessons.title: 113. Comparing with 比
lessons.subtitle: A 比 B + adjective · 比 … 冷一点儿 · 比 … 冷多了

explanations.title: A is more … than B
explanations.body: 比 (bǐ) means “compared with”. Put it between the two things, and put the adjective last: A 比 B + adjective. 北京比上海冷 is “Beijing is colder than Shanghai”. Do not use 很 before the adjective in this pattern. To say how much more, add 一点儿 (yìdiǎnr, a little) or 多了 (duō le, much more) after the adjective.

rows: This year is a little hotter than last year.
Winter is much colder than autumn.
I am taller than my older sister.

explanations.title: Not as much as
explanations.body: To say “not more than”, put 不 before 比: A 不比 B + adjective. 我不比他高 means “I am not taller than him”. It simply denies the comparison. A longer way to say that A is less is 没有 (next lesson).

examples.text: 夏天比春天热。
examples.translation: xiàtiān bǐ chūntiān rè — Summer is hotter than spring.

examples.text: 这儿比那儿冷一点儿。
examples.translation: zhèr bǐ nàr lěng yìdiǎnr — It is a little colder here than there.

examples.text: 冬天比秋天冷多了。
examples.translation: dōngtiān bǐ qiūtiān lěng duō le — Winter is much colder than autumn.

examples.text: 你比我高吗？
examples.translation: nǐ bǐ wǒ gāo ma — Are you taller than me?

exercises.prompt: What does 北京比上海冷 say?
options: Beijing is as cold as Shanghai.

exercises.prompt: Can you say 北京比上海很冷?
exercises.explanation: No 很 in the 比 pattern.

exercises.prompt: What does 冬天比秋天冷多了 say?
options: Winter is a little colder than autumn.
Winter is much colder than autumn.
Winter is as cold as autumn.

exercises.prompt: What does 这儿比那儿冷一点儿 say?
options: It is a little colder here than there.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “I am taller than my sister”?
How do you say “I am not taller than him”?

exercises.promptTranslation: Beijing is colder than Shanghai.
It is a little colder here than there.
Winter is much colder than autumn.
I am not taller than him.

lessons.title: 114. Not as … as: 没有 … 这么 / 那么
lessons.subtitle: 上海没有北京这么冷 · 北京有上海那么热吗？

explanations.title: 没有 for “not as”
explanations.body: 没有 (méiyǒu) is the opposite of 比 for “less”. A 没有 B + adjective says “A is not as … as B”. 上海没有北京冷 is “Shanghai is not as cold as Beijing”. Add 这么 (zhème) or 那么 (nàme), “so, that”, before the adjective to give it force: 上海没有北京这么冷, with 这么 for something near the speaker and 那么 for something far.

rows: Shanghai is not as cold as Beijing.
Shanghai is not as cold as Beijing (that cold).
Summer is not as cold as winter.

explanations.title: Asking with 有
explanations.body: A positive question uses 有 (not 没有): 北京有上海那么热吗？ means “Is Beijing as hot as Shanghai?”, and the speaker often thinks the answer is no. You can also ask 有没有: 北京有没有上海那么热？

examples.text: 我老家没有这儿这么热。
examples.translation: wǒ lǎojiā méiyǒu zhèr zhème rè — My hometown is not as hot as here.

examples.text: 冬天没有秋天那么舒服。
examples.translation: dōngtiān méiyǒu qiūtiān nàme shūfu — Winter is not as comfortable as autumn.

examples.text: 北京有上海那么热吗？
examples.translation: běijīng yǒu shànghǎi nàme rè ma — Is Beijing as hot as Shanghai?

examples.text: 你们那儿有没有这儿这么冷？
examples.translation: nǐmen nàr yǒu méi yǒu zhèr zhème lěng — Is it as cold where you are as it is here?

options: not as … as, does not have
exercises.explanation: 没有 (méiyǒu) means “not as … as, does not have”.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 这么?
What does 上海没有北京冷 say?
options: Shanghai is as cold as Beijing.
Shanghai is not as cold as Beijing.

exercises.prompt: Which is the opposite of 比 for “less”?
exercises.explanation: 没有 means not as … as.

exercises.prompt: What does 夏天没有冬天那么冷 say?
options: Summer is not as cold as winter.
Summer is as cold as winter.

exercises.prompt: What does 北京有上海那么热吗？ ask?
options: Is Beijing as hot as Shanghai?
exercises.explanation: 有 … 那么 asks whether it reaches that degree.

exercises.prompt: When do you use 这么?
options: When the thing is near the speaker
exercises.explanation: 这 is near; 那 is far.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “My hometown is not as hot as here”?
options: 我老家不有这儿这么热。
我老家没这儿有这么热。
我老家这儿没有这么热。
我老家没有这儿这么热。
exercises.explanation: A 没有 B 这么 adjective.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask “Is it as cold there as here?”
options: 那儿没有有这儿这么冷？
那儿有没有冷这儿这么？
那儿有这儿没有这么冷？
那儿有没有这儿这么冷？
exercises.explanation: 有没有 + B + 这么 + adjective.

exercises.promptTranslation: Shanghai is not as cold as Beijing.
Summer is not as cold as winter.
My hometown is not as hot as here.

exercises.prompt: 北京___上海那么热吗？ (positive question)
exercises.promptTranslation: Is Beijing as hot as Shanghai?

lessons.title: 115. But: 可是
lessons.subtitle: 冬天很冷，可是我喜欢冬天

explanations.title: 可是 joins two ideas
explanations.body: 可是 (kěshì) means “but” and starts the second clause: 冬天很冷，可是我喜欢冬天. It does not need a partner like 因为 … 所以 …. Use it when the second part goes against what you would expect from the first. It is spoken and written equally, and 但是 (dànshì) means the same.

rows: 夏天很热，可是我喜欢夏天。
Summer is hot, but I like summer.
他是南方人，可是他不喜欢热。
He is a southerner, but he does not like heat.
This place is not big, but it has many people.

explanations.title: Opposite ideas
explanations.body: A 可是 sentence sets two things against each other. If the second part just adds to the first, use 也 or 和 instead.

examples.text: 我老家不大，可是很舒服。
examples.translation: wǒ lǎojiā bú dà, kěshì hěn shūfu — My hometown is not big, but it is very comfortable.

examples.text: 冬天下大雪，可是我不能滑雪。
examples.translation: dōngtiān xià dà xuě, kěshì wǒ bù néng huáxuě — It snows heavily in winter, but I cannot ski.

examples.text: 他的中文很好，可是他不是中国人。
examples.translation: tā de zhōngwén hěn hǎo, kěshì tā bú shì zhōngguó rén — His Chinese is very good, but he is not Chinese.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 可是?
What does 冬天很冷，可是我喜欢冬天 say?
options: Winter is cold because I like it.
Winter is cold, but I like winter.
Winter is cold, so I like winter.
I like winter, and it is cold.
At the start of the second clause
Before the subject of the first clause

exercises.prompt: Does 可是 need a partner?
Which word means the same as 可是?

options: 夏天很热，可是我喜欢夏天。
夏天很热，所以我喜欢夏天。

exercises.prompt: What does 这儿不大，可是人很多 say?
options: This place is not big, but it has many people.
This place is big and has many people.
This place is not big, so it has few people.

exercises.promptTranslation: Summer is hot, but I like summer.

exercises.prompt: 他的中文很好，可___他不是中国人。
exercises.promptTranslation: His Chinese is very good, but he is not Chinese.
My hometown is not big, but it is very comfortable.

exercises.prompt: 冬天下大雪，可是我不___滑雪。
exercises.promptTranslation: It snows heavily in winter, but I cannot ski.

lessons.title: 116. Good to …: 好 + verb
lessons.subtitle: 好吃 · 好看 · 好听 · 好玩 · 好用

explanations.title: 好 before a verb
explanations.body: 好 (hǎo) before certain verbs makes an adjective meaning “good to …”, “pleasant to …”: 好吃 (hǎochī) is “tasty”, 好看 (hǎokàn) “nice to look at”, 好听 (hǎotīng) “nice to hear”, 好玩 (hǎowán) “fun” and 好用 (hǎoyòng) “easy to use”. These are adjectives, so 很 can go in front: 很好吃. Do not confuse these with 天气好, “the weather is good”, where 好 is just an adjective on its own.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Say what the thing is, then the 好 word with 很.

examples.text: 这个饺子很好吃。
examples.translation: zhè gè jiǎozi hěn hǎochī — These dumplings are very tasty.

examples.text: 这个城市很好玩。
examples.translation: zhè gè chéngshì hěn hǎowán — This city is a lot of fun.

examples.text: 春天的天气很好，花很好看。
examples.translation: chūntiān de tiānqì hěn hǎo, huā hěn hǎokàn — The weather in spring is nice and the flowers are pretty.

examples.text: 这个手机好用吗？
examples.translation: zhè gè shǒujī hǎoyòng ma — Is this phone easy to use?

examples.text: 这首歌很好听。
examples.translation: zhè shǒu gē hěn hǎotīng — This song is nice to listen to.

exercises.explanation: 好听 (hǎotīng) means “nice to listen to”.

exercises.prompt: How do you read 好听?
How do you read 好玩?
Can 很 go before 好吃?
What does 这个城市很好玩 say?
options: This city is good at playing.
This city is a lot of fun.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “These dumplings are very tasty”?
How do you ask “Is this phone easy to use?”

exercises.promptTranslation: These dumplings are very tasty.
This city is a lot of fun.
The flowers in spring are pretty.

exercises.explanation: 好听 is nice to listen to.
exercises.promptTranslation: This song is nice to listen to.

lessons.title: 117. Review: seasons and weather
lessons.subtitle: 季节 · 天气 · 因为…所以 · 不…也不… · 比 · 一样 · 没有 · 可是

explanations.title: What you can now do
explanations.body: You can name the seasons, describe weather and temperature, give reasons, compare two things and contrast ideas. These questions mix them.

examples.text: 我最喜欢秋天，因为秋天不冷也不热。
examples.translation: wǒ zuì xǐhuan qiūtiān, yīnwèi qiūtiān bù lěng yě bú rè — I like autumn best because it is neither cold nor hot.

examples.text: 冬天比秋天冷多了，可是可以滑雪。
examples.translation: dōngtiān bǐ qiūtiān lěng duō le, kěshì kěyǐ huáxuě — Winter is much colder than autumn, but we can ski.

examples.text: 上海没有北京这么冷。
examples.translation: shànghǎi méiyǒu běijīng zhème lěng — Shanghai is not as cold as Beijing.

Which means “Winter is colder than autumn”?

Complete: 夏天很热，___我喜欢夏天。
我最喜欢秋天，因为秋天不冷___不热。
exercises.promptTranslation: I like autumn best because it is neither cold nor hot.
Winter is much colder than autumn.

units.title: 第五课 Provinces and states

lessons.title: 118. How China is divided
lessons.subtitle: 省 · 自治区 · 直辖市 · 特别行政区 · 省会

explanations.title: Four kinds of division
explanations.body: China’s first-level divisions come in four kinds. A 省 (shěng) is a province, and its capital is a 省会 (shěnghuì). A 自治区 (zìzhìqū) is an autonomous region, “self-governing area”, and its capital is a 首府 (shǒufǔ). A 直辖市 (zhíxiáshì) is a municipality under the central government, and a 特别行政区 (tèbié xíngzhèngqū) is a special administrative region. A city is a 市 (shì). The 省 or 市 is often dropped in speech: 四川 for 四川省, 成都 for 成都市.

explanations.title: Municipalities and special regions
explanations.body: Four big cities are directly under the central government: 北京 (Běijīng), 天津 (Tiānjīn), 上海 (Shànghǎi) and 重庆 (Chóngqìng). There are two special administrative regions: 香港 (Xiānggǎng, Hong Kong) and 澳门 (Àomén, Macau). Their full names end in 特别行政区.

examples.text: 四川是中国的一个省。
examples.translation: sìchuān shì zhōngguó de yí gè shěng — Sichuan is a province of China.

examples.text: 成都是四川的省会。
examples.translation: chéngdū shì sìchuān de shěnghuì — Chengdu is the capital of Sichuan.

examples.text: 上海是直辖市。
examples.translation: shànghǎi shì zhíxiáshì — Shanghai is a municipality directly under the central government.

explanations.title: Full names and notes (from the book)
explanations.body: The book writes each place with its type: 辽宁省 (Liáoníng Shěng), the capital 沈阳市 (Shěnyáng Shì), the municipality 北京市 (Běijīng Shì), the autonomous region 西藏自治区 (Xīzàng Zìzhìqū). The two special administrative regions have long full names: 香港特别行政区 (Xiānggǎng Tèbiéxíngzhèngqū) and 澳门特别行政区 (Àomén Tèbiéxíngzhèngqū). Notes: 1. In colloquial conversation the word 省 or 市 is often omitted. 2. 香港特别行政区 and 澳门特别行政区 are often shortened to 香港行政特区 or 香港特区, and 澳门行政特区 or 澳门特区.

explanations.title: Twelve provinces and their capitals
explanations.body: Say a province and its 省会 together: 辽宁省 (Liáoníng Shěng), capital 沈阳市. In speech people drop 省 and 市. Learn them in the order they are listed here, from the northeast down the coast to the south.

explanations.title: 山西 and 陕西, the tone pair
explanations.body: Two provinces sound almost the same: 山西 is Shānxī (first tone, west of the mountains) and 陕西 is Shǎnxī (third tone, whose capital is 西安). The only difference is the tone of the first syllable.

explanations.title: Eleven more provinces
explanations.body: These provinces run through the middle, the southwest and the northwest, and finish with the southern coast. Their capitals work the same way: name + 的省会 + capital.

explanations.title: Five autonomous regions
explanations.body: The five autonomous regions have a 首府 instead of a 省会: 内蒙古 (Nèiměnggǔ), 广西 (Guǎngxī), 西藏 (Xīzàng), 宁夏 (Níngxià) and 新疆 (Xīnjiāng). The full name ends in 自治区, and the longer names carry the people’s name too, but the short form is what you use.

lessons.title: 121. American states in Chinese
lessons.subtitle: 美国 · 州 · 加利福尼亚 · 纽约 · 德克萨斯 · 华盛顿

explanations.title: Foreign names by sound
explanations.body: 美国 (Měiguó) is the USA, “the beautiful country”, and a state is a 州 (zhōu). Most American state and city names are written in Chinese by their sound, so the characters are chosen for sound, not meaning. They can be long, and many have a short form: 加利福尼亚 is shortened to 加州 and 德克萨斯 to 德州.

explanations.title: Cities and a question
explanations.body: City names follow the same method: 蒙特雷 is Monterey, 旧金山 is San Francisco (it means “old gold mountain”) and 洛杉矶 is Los Angeles. 华盛顿 is the name of a state and of the capital of the USA; the context tells you which one.

examples.translation: méngtèléi zài jiālìfúníyà zhōu — Monterey is in the state of California.

lessons.title: 122. A proverb: 边学边问，才有学问
lessons.subtitle: 边 … 边 … · 才 · 学问

explanations.title: Doing two things at once
explanations.body: 边 … 边 … (biān … biān …) joins two actions that happen together: 边走边说 is “talk while walking”. Put 边 before each verb. The two verbs are both actions and the subject is the same person. 边学边问 is “learn while asking”.

explanations.title: The whole proverb
explanations.body: 边学边问，才有学问。 means “Learn while you ask, and only then will you have knowledge”. 才 (cái) here says that a result comes only on one condition. 学问 (xuéwen) is learning or scholarship, and uses 问 (wèn, ask) as part of the word, because asking is the way to learn.

examples.text: 边学边问，才有学问。
examples.translation: biān xué biān wèn, cái yǒu xuéwèn — Learn while asking, and only then will you have learning.

examples.text: 他喜欢边走边说。
examples.translation: tā xǐhuan biān zǒu biān shuō — He likes to talk while walking.

examples.text: 我们边学中文边问老师。
examples.translation: wǒmen biān xué zhōngwén biān wèn lǎoshī — We ask the teacher while learning Chinese.
