lessons.title: 383. Lesson 15 Presentation 3 grammar: the V + 来 + V + 去 construction
lessons.subtitle: 飞来飞去 · 挑来选去 · 走来走去 · 想来想去

explanations.title: The V + 来 + V + 去 construction
explanations.body: This construction indicates that an action happens repeatedly or moves back and forth. It is generally used with two verbs that are either identical or synonymous, for example 飞来飞去 and 挑来选去. Subject + V + 来 + V + 去. (Note: if the verb has an object, the object is usually at the beginning of the sentence.)

examples.text: 很多鸟在天上飞来飞去。
examples.translation: hěn duō niǎo zài tiān shàng fēi lái fēi qù — Many birds fly back and forth in the sky.

examples.text: 他看来看去，都看不出那位医生写了什么。
examples.translation: tā kàn lái kàn qù dōu kàn bù chū nà wèi yī shēng xiě le shén me — He looked this way and that, but could not make out what the doctor had written.

examples.text: 我不喜欢靠过道的座位，因为总有人在旁边走来走去。
examples.translation: wǒ bù xǐ huān kào guò dào de zuò wèi yīn wèi zǒng yǒu rén zài páng biān zǒu lái zǒu qù — I don’t like aisle seats, because there are always people walking back and forth next to them.

examples.text: 他把沙发搬来搬去，也没找到合适的地方。
examples.translation: tā bǎ shā fā bān lái bān qù yě méi zhǎo dào hé shì de dì fāng — He moved the sofa around, but still didn’t find a suitable place.

examples.text: 这件事他想来想去，不知道应该怎么办。
examples.translation: zhè jiàn shì tā xiǎng lái xiǎng qù bù zhī dào yīng gāi zěn me bàn — He thought it over and over, and didn’t know what to do.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: Work in pairs to rewrite the following sentences using the V + 来 + V + 去 construction. The originals: 爸爸做了很多菜，她尝尝这个，又尝尝那个，还是觉得烤鸭最好吃。 早上很多人在公园里来回走路。 这句话我听了一遍又一遍，还是听不懂。 我在公共汽车站等了很长时间，还是没有车过来。 这些肉他烤了又烤。因为烤得时间太长，已经不好吃了。 The book leaves the rewritten column empty; my rewrites (mine):

examples.text: 爸爸做了很多菜，她尝来尝去，还是觉得烤鸭最好吃。
examples.translation: bà bà zuò le hěn duō cài tā cháng lái cháng qù hái shì jué de kǎo yā zuì hǎo chī — Dad made many dishes; she tasted this and that, and still felt the roast duck was the best. (mine)

examples.text: 早上很多人在公园里走来走去。
examples.translation: zǎo shàng hěn duō rén zài gōng yuán lǐ zǒu lái zǒu qù — In the morning many people walk back and forth in the park. (mine)

examples.text: 这句话我听来听去，还是听不懂。
examples.translation: zhè jù huà wǒ tīng lái tīng qù hái shì tīng bù dǒng — I listened to this sentence over and over and still couldn’t understand it. (mine)

examples.text: 我在公共汽车站等来等去，还是没有车过来。
examples.translation: wǒ zài gōng gòng qì chē zhàn děng lái děng qù hái shì méi yǒu chē guò lái — I waited at the bus stop for a long time and still no bus came. (mine)

examples.text: 这些肉他烤来烤去。因为烤得时间太长，已经不好吃了。
examples.translation: zhè xiē ròu tā kǎo lái kǎo qù yīn wèi kǎo de shí jiān tài cháng yǐ jīng bù hǎo chī le — He grilled this meat over and over. Because it was grilled for too long, it’s no longer tasty. (mine)

lessons.title: 384. Lesson 15 Presentation 3 grammar: the 不…不… construction
lessons.subtitle: 不大不小 · 不冷不热 · 不急不慢 · 不快不慢地散步

explanations.title: The 不…不… construction
explanations.body: The 不…不… construction is used to express that neither A nor B are true; in colloquial Chinese it is often used to indicate a desirable state, such as 这双皮鞋不大不小 (neither too big nor too small) or 蒙特雷的天气不冷不热 (not too cold, not too hot). 不…不… + 的 + Noun (Noun Phrase). 不…不… + 地 + Verb (Verb Phrase).

examples.text: 这部电影不长不短。
examples.translation: zhè bù diàn yǐng bù cháng bù duǎn — This movie is neither long nor short.

examples.text: 这个房子不大不小。
examples.translation: zhè ge fáng zi bú dà bù xiǎo — This house is neither big nor small.

examples.text: 他是一个做事不急不慢的人。
examples.translation: tā shì yí gè zuò shì bù jí bú màn de rén — He is a person who does things neither hurriedly nor slowly.

examples.text: 爸爸给他买了一张不高不矮的书桌。
examples.translation: bà bà gěi tā mǎi le yì zhāng bù gāo bù ǎi de shū zhuō — Dad bought him a desk that is neither tall nor short.

examples.text: 小李说话不快不慢。
examples.translation: xiǎo lǐ shuō huà bú kuài bú màn — Xiao Li speaks neither fast nor slow.

examples.text: 老王不言不语地看着电视。
examples.translation: lǎo wáng bù yán bù yǔ de kàn zhe diàn shì — Lao Wang watched TV without saying a word.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading, Writing, and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. In the passage the book gives, fill in the blanks with the words provided in parentheses using the 不…不… construction: 高、矮; 胖、瘦; 早、晚; 大、小; 多、少; 快、慢; 大、小; 远、近. B. Answer the questions: 1. 王丽长得什么样？ 2. 王丽什么时候去的电影院？ 3. 他们的晚饭吃得怎么样？ 4. 吃完晚饭以后他们做什么了？ (Mine: 不高不矮，不胖不瘦，爱笑; 三点半; 菜有点儿咸，但味道不错，四个菜八十元; 去海边不快不慢地散步，然后小李送她回公寓.) C. Check your work against the complete passage:

examples.text: 小李的女朋友王丽今年二十四岁，长得不高不矮，不胖不瘦，说话的时候总是笑。今天小李和她去看了一场电影。他们约好三点半在电影院门口见面，可是小李三点就在电影院门口等。王丽呢，不早不晚三点半到那儿。看完电影，小李带王丽去一家不大不小的饭馆吃晚饭。那儿的菜虽然有点儿咸，但味道不错。他们点了四个菜，花了不多不少八十元钱。吃完饭，他们又到了海边，不快不慢地散了一会儿步。然后，小李送王丽回到她那套不大不小离海边不远不近的公寓。
examples.translation: xiǎo lǐ de nǚ péng yǒu wáng lì jīn nián èr shí sì suì zhǎng de bù gāo bù ǎi bú pàng bú shòu shuō huà de shí hòu zǒng shì xiào jīn tiān xiǎo lǐ hé tā qù kàn le yì cháng diàn yǐng tā men yuē hǎo sān diǎn bàn zài diàn yǐng yuàn mén kǒu jiàn miàn kě shì xiǎo lǐ sān diǎn jiù zài diàn yǐng yuàn mén kǒu děng wáng lì ne bù zǎo bù wǎn sān diǎn bàn dào nàr kàn wán diàn yǐng xiǎo lǐ dài wáng lì qù yì jiā bú dà bù xiǎo de fàn guǎn chī wǎn fàn nàr de cài suī rán yǒu diǎnr xián dàn wèi dào bú cuò tā men diǎn le sì gè cài huā le bù duō bù shǎo bā shí yuán qián chī wán fàn tā men yòu dào le hǎi biān bú kuài bú màn de sàn le yí huìr bù rán hòu xiǎo lǐ sòng wáng lì huí dào tā nà tào bú dà bù xiǎo lí hǎi biān bù yuǎn bú jìn de gōng yù — Xiao Li’s girlfriend Wang Li is twenty-four this year; she is neither tall nor short, neither fat nor thin, and always smiles when she talks. Today Xiao Li and she went to see a movie. They had agreed to meet at the movie theater entrance at three thirty, but Xiao Li was already waiting there at three. Wang Li arrived there neither early nor late, at three thirty. After the movie, Xiao Li took Wang Li to a restaurant that was neither big nor small for dinner. Although the food there was a bit salty, the taste was good. They ordered four dishes, which cost exactly eighty yuan. After eating they went to the seaside and took a walk neither fast nor slow. Then Xiao Li took Wang Li back to her apartment, which is neither big nor small and neither far nor near the sea.

lessons.title: 385. Lesson 15 Presentation 3 grammar: the adverbial modifier marker 地
lessons.subtitle: 高兴地告诉我 · 慢慢地走 · 你跑得很慢 vs. 你慢慢地跑过去

explanations.title: The adverbial modifier marker 地
explanations.body: An adverb is a part of speech that modifies (i.e., describes) a verb. When an adverb describes the manner of a verb, it is often formed with an adjective and marked by the adverbial modifier 地. Example: 小王高兴地告诉我，她考上北京大学了。 An adverbial expression is different from a complement expression. A complement expression is descriptive in nature, whereas an adverbial expression tells the “attitude” or manner of an action. Also, a complement is most often used in connection with a habitual action, or an action that has already taken place, whereas an adverbial modifier may also refer to an action that has yet to happen. Example: 你跑得很慢 vs. 你慢慢地跑过去。 Adjective + 地 + Verb (+ Object).

examples.text: 小王高兴地告诉我，她考上北京大学了。

examples.text: 他开心地笑了。

lessons.title: 386. Lesson 15 Presentation 3 grammar: the aspect particle 着
lessons.subtitle: 客厅里摆着沙发 · 带着孩子们踢球 · 忙着收拾垃圾 · 笑着说

explanations.title: The aspect particle 着
explanations.body: The aspect particle 着 appears after a verb indicating the state or continuation of an action in a static mode. Example: 大明在院子里站着；客厅里放着一张沙发。 We can use the pattern verb + 着 to modify the following verb, thus indicating the state or manner in which the action is carried out. Example: 她坐着讲课。 In Lesson 10 Presentation 3 we learned: 客厅里摆着一张三人沙发。主卧室里面放着一张双人床。后院种着很多果树。 In the current presentation: 爸爸们又带着孩子们踢球，而妈妈们忙着收拾垃圾。 In all these sentences, the aspect particle 着 appears after a verb indicating continuation, either a) indicating an existing state, such as sentences 1 to 3; or b) indicating the manner of carrying out an action, such as sentences 4 and 5. Manner and action: 带着孩子们 (taking the kids) + 踢球 (to play soccer); 忙着 (being busy) + 收拾垃圾 (to clean up). *着 can also be a suffix for some words to form a preposition, such as 沿着 in this presentation.

examples.text: 客厅里摆着一张三人沙发。
examples.translation: kè tīng lǐ bǎi zhe yì zhāng sān rén shā fā — In the living room is placed a three-person sofa.

examples.text: 主卧室里面放着一张双人床。

examples.text: 大明在院子里站着。

examples.text: 他穿着军服。

explanations.title: Patterns and examples
explanations.body: Affirmative: Subject + Verb + 着; Subject + Verb + 着 + Verb (+ Object). Negative: Subject + 不/没有 + verb + 着 (+ Object); Subject + 不是/没有 + verb + 着 + Verb (+ Object). Interrogative: Subject + Verb + 着 + 吗？; Subject + Verb + 着 + Verb (+ Object) + 吗？ Affirmative-Negative: Subject + 有没有/是不是 + verb + 着？; Subject + 有没有/是不是 + Verb + 着 + Verb (+ Object)？ The eight examples:

examples.text: 李老师在教室里坐着。
examples.translation: lǐ lǎo shī zài jiào shì lǐ zuò zhe — Teacher Li is sitting in the classroom.

examples.text: 教室里放着四张桌子和十把椅子。

lessons.title: 387. Lesson 15 Presentation 3 grammar: the (一)直到…才… construction

explanations.title: The (一)直到…才… construction
explanations.body: This construction expresses the idea of “not until….” Example: 昨天他一直到十点才回家。 Affirmative: (一)直到 + Time/Event + Subject + 才…; Subject + (一)直到 + Time/Event + 才… Negative: (一)直到 + Time/Event + Subject + 都/还 + 不/没…; Subject + (一)直到 + Time/Event + 都/还 + 不/没… The eight examples (the book prints them in two columns, 1 to 8; the first example is repeated at the end):

examples.text: 昨天晚上一直到十点半我才做完作业。

examples.text: 昨天晚上我一直到十点半才做完作业。
examples.translation: zuó tiān wǎn shàng wǒ yì zhí dào shí diǎn bàn cái zuò wán zuò yè — Last night I didn’t finish my homework until ten thirty.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading, Speaking, and Writing): Erlin’s email
explanations.body: A. Read the email below (the book prints TO, CC and Subject lines empty). Look up any unfamiliar words, then answer in English: 1. Why did Erlin write this message? 2. How did his family in China celebrate Chinese New Year? 3. What did the Chinese community do to celebrate Chinese New Year on Sunday? 4. What did Erlin, his wife, and children do respectively for the gathering? (Mine: to say Happy New Year to his parents and tell them about his celebration; over ten people gathered, eating, drinking, talking and laughing; they gathered in the school auditorium, each bringing dishes, drinks, fruit and dessert, with performances; Erlin made red-braised pork and boiled fish, Pingping organized the performances, and the children danced.) B. Pair up and compare; ask each other three questions in Chinese about the details. C. Work with your partner to rewrite the passage as a dialog between Erlin and his father (five exchanges) and act it out.

examples.text: 爸爸、妈妈过年好！刚才看到爸爸发来的视频。全家十几口人在一起过年，又吃又喝又说又笑，真热闹。爸爸、妈妈的身体看上去也不错，太好了！美国加州春节不放假，但今年春节是个星期天，大家不上班，很多华人朋友在我们学校的礼堂聚了聚。那天，大家每个人都带了一两个菜，还准备了各种饮料、水果、甜点。我做了一个红烧肉，还有一个水煮鱼，大家都很喜欢。那天最忙的要数您儿媳萍萍了。她组织了一些朋友给大家表演节目。有的唱歌，有的跳舞，很受欢迎。我最喜欢的节目是孩子们的舞蹈，里面也有您的孙子和孙女。看他们在舞台上高兴地跳来跳去，觉得特别开心。聚会从中午十二点开始，一直到下午四点才结束。明年我和萍萍打算带着两个孩子回老家，和爸爸妈妈还有其他家人一起过年。多多保重！您的儿媳、孙子、孙女也祝您身体健康！二林
examples.translation: bà bà mā mā guò nián hǎo gāng cái kàn dào bà bà fā lái de shì pín quán jiā shí jǐ kǒu rén zài yì qǐ guò nián yòu chī yòu hē yòu shuō yòu xiào zhēn rè nào bà bà mā mā de shēn tǐ kàn shàng qù yě bú cuò tài hǎo le měi guó jiā zhōu chūn jié bú fàng jià dàn jīn nián chūn jié shì gè xīng qī tiān dà jiā bú shàng bān hěn duō huá rén péng yǒu zài wǒ men xué xiào de lǐ táng jù le jù nà tiān dà jiā měi gè rén dōu dài le yì liǎng gè cài hái zhǔn bèi le gè zhǒng yǐn liào shuǐ guǒ tián diǎn wǒ zuò le yí gè hóng shāo ròu hái yǒu yí gè shuǐ zhǔ yú dà jiā dōu hěn xǐ huān nà tiān zuì máng de yào shǔ nín ér xí píng píng le tā zǔ zhī le yì xiē péng yǒu gěi dà jiā biǎo yǎn jié mù yǒu de chàng gē yǒu de tiào wǔ hěn shòu huān yíng wǒ zuì xǐ huān de jié mù shì hái zi men de wǔ dǎo lǐ miàn yě yǒu nín de sūn zi hé sūn nǚ kàn tā men zài wǔ tái shàng gāo xìng de tiào lái tiào qù jué de tè bié kāi xīn jù huì cóng zhōng wǔ shí èr diǎn kāi shǐ yì zhí dào xià wǔ sì diǎn cái jié shù míng nián wǒ hé píng píng dǎ suàn dài zhe liǎng gè hái zi huí lǎo jiā hé bà bà mā mā hái yǒu qí tā jiā rén yì qǐ guò nián duō duō bǎo zhòng nín de ér xí sūn zi sūn nǚ yě zhù nín shēn tǐ jiàn kāng èr lín — Dad and Mom, happy New Year! I just saw the video Dad sent. The whole family, over ten people, spent the New Year together, eating, drinking, talking and laughing; so lively. Dad and Mom look well too, which is great! In California, the US, there is no holiday for Spring Festival, but this year Spring Festival was on a Sunday and nobody was at work, so many Chinese friends gathered in our school’s auditorium. That day everyone brought one or two dishes, and there were also all kinds of drinks, fruit and desserts. I made a red-braised pork and a boiled fish, which everyone liked. The busiest that day was your daughter-in-law Pingping. She organized some friends to perform for everyone. Some sang, some danced, and it was very popular. My favorite item was the children’s dance, which included your grandson and granddaughter. Watching them jump around happily on the stage, I felt especially happy. The party started at twelve noon and did not end until four in the afternoon. Next year Pingping and I plan to take our two children back to our hometown to spend the New Year with you and our other family. Take good care! Your daughter-in-law, grandson and granddaughter also wish you good health! Erlin

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening, Reading, and Speaking): Sun Laoshi’s email
explanations.body: Last Wednesday your class had a very successful picnic. You invited both Sun Laoshi and Gao Laoshi, but only Sun was able to attend. A. Both teachers contacted you after the event. In pairs, you read Sun Laoshi’s email (subject 孙老师的邮件), and your partner listens to Gao Laoshi’s message (audio, not included). B. Share the main idea of your message with your partner and write down what you heard; to double-check, read the script of Gao Laoshi’s message while your partner reads Sun Laoshi’s email, and give each other feedback. C. Work together to write an email to Gao Laoshi (subject 给高老师的邮件) and describe what happened at the picnic last Wednesday; include the EEIs plus information about the weather, food, and what attendees were talking about. D. Share your email with the class.

examples.text: 马龙：你好！谢谢你邀请我参加星期三的聚会！很长时间没见到同学们，这次见面，发现大家的中文比以前更好了，我非常高兴。那天的活动组织得真不错。我在系里开会一直开到十一点半才过去，到那儿一看，啊，你们准备了那么多又好吃又好看的菜，还有各种饮料和水果，太棒了！我特别喜欢同学们做的苹果派，王老师做的牛肉也好吃，很受欢迎。西瓜是你买的吧？那么甜，我吃了可不少呢。大家坐着边吃边聊，都是讲中文。看来同学们都喜欢学中文，学习也很努力，这是让老师们最开心的事儿。很高兴见到你太太和你们的儿子。你儿子我以前见过，这次又看到他，发现这孩子比上次高了很多，也更可爱了。再次感谢你邀请我参加这次活动！孙老师
examples.translation: mǎ lóng nǐ hǎo xiè xiè nǐ yāo qǐng wǒ cān jiā xīng qī sān de jù huì hěn cháng shí jiān méi jiàn dào tóng xué men zhè cì jiàn miàn fā xiàn dà jiā de zhōng wén bǐ yǐ qián gèng hǎo le wǒ fēi cháng gāo xìng nà tiān de huó dòng zǔ zhī de zhēn bú cuò wǒ zài xì lǐ kāi huì yì zhí kāi dào shí yī diǎn bàn cái guò qù dào nàr yí kàn a nǐ men zhǔn bèi le nà me duō yòu hǎo chī yòu hǎo kàn de cài hái yǒu gè zhǒng yǐn liào hé shuǐ guǒ tài bàng le wǒ tè bié xǐ huān tóng xué men zuò de píng guǒ pài wáng lǎo shī zuò de niú ròu yě hǎo chī hěn shòu huān yíng xī guā shì nǐ mǎi de ba nà me tián wǒ chī le kě bù shǎo ne dà jiā zuò zhe biān chī biān liáo dōu shì jiǎng zhōng wén kàn lái tóng xué men dōu xǐ huān xué zhōng wén xué xí yě hěn nǔ lì zhè shì ràng lǎo shī men zuì kāi xīn de shì ér hěn gāo xìng jiàn dào nǐ tài tài hé nǐ men de ér zi nǐ ér zi wǒ yǐ qián jiàn guò zhè cì yòu kàn dào tā fā xiàn zhè hái zi bǐ shàng cì gāo le hěn duō yě gèng kě ài le zài cì gǎn xiè nǐ yāo qǐng wǒ cān jiā zhè cì huó dòng sūn lǎo shī — Ma Long: Hello! Thank you for inviting me to Wednesday’s gathering! I hadn’t seen the students for a long time; meeting this time, I found everyone’s Chinese better than before, and I’m very happy. The event was really well organized. My meeting at the department went on until eleven thirty before I could come over; when I got there, ah, you had prepared so many delicious and good-looking dishes, plus all kinds of drinks and fruit; wonderful! I especially liked the apple pie the students made, and the beef Teacher Wang made was also tasty and popular. The watermelon was bought by you, right? So sweet; I ate quite a lot. Everyone sat eating and chatting while speaking Chinese. It seems the students all like learning Chinese and study very hard, which is what makes teachers happiest. I was very glad to see your wife and your son. I had seen your son before; seeing him again this time, I found he is much taller than last time and cuter. Thank you again for inviting me to this event! Teacher Sun

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Writing, Reading, and Speaking): the potluck
explanations.body: You are a graduate student at Shenzhen University in China; the president of the Graduate Student Club wants you to help organize an American-style potluck during the coming weekend. A. First, listen to an audio file you found online, then write in Chinese a brief description of potlucks in the United States (audio, not included). B. The potluck took place yesterday. You want to write an article for the Graduate Students Newsletter about the event (title 我们的百乐餐). Use your past experiences and imagination. The following passage may also help. C. Share your work in pairs.

examples.text: 前几天同学老王打来电话，说小钱从美国回来了，想和老同学们一起吃个饭。我说，这次不去饭店吃了，咱们去海边来一次百乐餐怎么样？老王说，好啊，你来组织吧。我马上发邮件给每个同学，告诉他们我的计划，请他们到时候每人带一个菜去海边。老王准备喝的东西，我准备餐具和甜点。聚会那天，我早早地坐公共汽车到了海边，发现有一半的同学早就到了。他们边喝茶边聊天，十分热闹。小钱和他太太也在，还给大家带来了美国巧克力。一会儿大家就都到了，各种各样的饭菜放在一起，差不多有二十个，有鱼、牛肉、猪肉、素菜……，还有饺子和面条。我买了一个大蛋糕，老王带了啤酒、葡萄酒和饮料。大家边吃边聊天，说了很多上大学时候的事。最后，小钱说，欢迎大家明年去美国，到加州玩儿几天。到时候，他会请大家到他们家吃烤肉，大家一起热闹热闹。
examples.translation: qián jǐ tiān tóng xué lǎo wáng dǎ lái diàn huà shuō xiǎo qián cóng měi guó huí lái le xiǎng hé lǎo tóng xué men yì qǐ chī gè fàn wǒ shuō zhè cì bú qù fàn diàn chī le zán men qù hǎi biān lái yí cì bǎi lè cān zěn me yàng lǎo wáng shuō hǎo a nǐ lái zǔ zhī ba wǒ mǎ shàng fā yóu jiàn gěi měi gè tóng xué gào sù tā men wǒ de jì huà qǐng tā men dào shí hòu měi rén dài yí gè cài qù hǎi biān lǎo wáng zhǔn bèi hē de dōng xī wǒ zhǔn bèi cān jù hé tián diǎn jù huì nà tiān wǒ zǎo zǎo de zuò gōng gòng qì chē dào le hǎi biān fā xiàn yǒu yí bàn de tóng xué zǎo jiù dào le tā men biān hē chá biān liáo tiān shí fēn rè nào xiǎo qián hé tā tài tài yě zài hái gěi dà jiā dài lái le měi guó qiǎo kè lì yí huìr dà jiā jiù dōu dào le gè zhǒng gè yàng de fàn cài fàng zài yì qǐ chà bu duō yǒu èr shí gè yǒu yú niú ròu zhū ròu sù cài hái yǒu jiǎo zi hé miàn tiáo wǒ mǎi le yí gè dà dàn gāo lǎo wáng dài le pí jiǔ pú táo jiǔ hé yǐn liào dà jiā biān chī biān liáo tiān shuō le hěn duō shàng dà xué shí hòu de shì zuì hòu xiǎo qián shuō huān yíng dà jiā míng nián qù měi guó dào jiā zhōu wánr jǐ tiān dào shí hòu tā huì qǐng dà jiā dào tā men jiā chī kǎo ròu dà jiā yì qǐ rè nào rè nào — A few days ago my classmate Lao Wang called and said Xiao Qian had come back from the US and wanted to have a meal with old classmates. I said, this time let’s not eat at a restaurant; how about having a potluck by the sea? Lao Wang said, good, you organize it. I immediately emailed every classmate to tell them my plan and ask each to bring a dish to the seaside. Lao Wang would prepare the drinks and I would prepare tableware and dessert. On the day of the gathering I took the bus early to the seaside and found that half of the classmates had arrived long before. They were drinking tea and chatting; very lively. Xiao Qian and his wife were also there and had brought American chocolate for everyone. Soon everybody had arrived; all kinds of food were put together, almost twenty dishes, including fish, beef, pork, vegetables…, as well as dumplings and noodles. I bought a big cake, and Lao Wang brought beer, wine and drinks. Everyone ate and chatted and talked about many things from their university days. In the end Xiao Qian said, everyone is welcome to come to the US next year and play for a few days in California. By then he will invite everyone to his home to have a barbecue and have fun together.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Writing and Speaking): the Chinese New Year report
explanations.body: The local Chinese community celebrated the Chinese New Year last Saturday, and you did your part by helping to prepare a flyer in Chinese for the event. A. Below is a report about the event in the local newspaper. Write a summary in Chinese to share with your classmates, including the EEIs plus several important details. The report: “Around 500 people crowded the Monterey Community Center on Saturday afternoon to celebrate the Chinese New Year, with Monterey’s Mayor as special guest. The event started at 11:30. Speaking at the celebration, Mayor Smith congratulated the Chinese community on the arrival of the Chinese New Year, and he also thanked them for their contribution to the local community. Following the speeches were cultural performances. The performers sang songs and performed traditional Chinese dances. The audience loved the performances so much that they kept cheering and applauding, especially for those done by students from DLI. The organizers ordered food from local Chinese restaurants, and many participants brought their home-made food as well. One elderly lady, Mrs. Liu, brought dumplings she had made. She told the reporter that people in her hometown have to eat dumplings on Chinese New Year’s Eve. The celebrations ended around 3:30 pm. Monterey has been hosting annual celebrations of Chinese Lunar New Year for the last seven years.” B. Pair up and, in Chinese, ask each other about the event. (Pictures, not included.) My Chinese summary:

examples.text: 星期六下午，大约五百人来到蒙特雷社区中心庆祝春节，市长是特别客人。活动十一点半开始，市长向华人社区祝贺春节，也感谢他们对本地社区的贡献。接着是文化表演，大家唱歌，跳传统舞蹈，观众不停地欢呼鼓掌，特别是学生们的表演。主办方在当地的中餐馆订了菜，很多人也带来了自己做的菜。刘奶奶带来了她包的饺子，她说她老家的人除夕一定要吃饺子。庆祝活动三点半左右结束。蒙特雷已经连续七年举办春节庆祝活动。
examples.translation: xīng qī liù xià wǔ dà yuē wǔ bǎi rén lái dào méng tè léi shè qū zhōng xīn qìng zhù chūn jié shì zhǎng shì tè bié kè rén huó dòng shí yī diǎn bàn kāi shǐ shì zhǎng xiàng huá rén shè qū zhù hè chūn jié yě gǎn xiè tā men duì běn dì shè qū de gòng xiàn jiē zhe shì wén huà biǎo yǎn dà jiā chàng gē tiào chuán tǒng wǔ dǎo guān zhòng bù tíng de huān hū gǔ zhǎng tè bié shì xué shēng men de biǎo yǎn zhǔ bàn fāng zài dāng dì de zhōng cān guǎn dìng le cài hěn duō rén yě dài lái le zì jǐ zuò de cài liú nǎi nǎi dài lái le tā bāo de jiǎo zi tā shuō tā lǎo jiā de rén chú xī yí dìng yào chī jiǎo zi qìng zhù huó dòng sān diǎn bàn zuǒ yòu jié shù méng tè léi yǐ jīng lián xù qī nián jǔ bàn chūn jié qìng zhù huó dòng — Mine: On Saturday afternoon about five hundred people came to Monterey Community Center to celebrate Chinese New Year, with the mayor as special guest. The event started at eleven thirty; the mayor congratulated the Chinese community and thanked it for its contribution. Next came cultural performances: singing and traditional dances, and the audience kept cheering and applauding, especially for the students. The organizers ordered food from local Chinese restaurants and many people brought home-made food. Mrs. Liu brought dumplings, saying people in her hometown must eat dumplings on New Year’s Eve. The event ended around three thirty. Monterey has hosted the celebration for seven years.

lessons.title: 391. Lesson 15 Area Studies: Invitations and Parties
lessons.subtitle: 邀请和聚会 · family celebrations · weddings · business receptions

explanations.title: Invitations and Parties
explanations.body: Like all cultures, the Chinese have parties and celebrations to mark rites of passage or important transitions and passages from one stage of life to another. These celebrations share the good fortune of families, promote the success of firms and reaffirm the value of traditions to Chinese both in China and overseas. In general, formal invitations are not very common for Chinese family celebrations, which include housewarming, birthdays, funerals, annual family get-togethers during the autumn, and spring festivals. This is not to say that anyone can attend the celebrations, but the custom of delivering a formal written invitation for family activities is less popular in China than it is in the U.S. Family celebrations are frequently coordinated by word of mouth, phone calls or text messaging. Formal business dinners and government-sponsored banquets, on the other hand, often use written invitations similar to those used in Western cultures. Whether it is an informal phone call or a formal invitation card, the information given is essentially the same. The invitee is informed of the special occasion, when and where the celebration will be held and (often) what to wear or bring. (Photographs, not included.)

explanations.title: Family parties and weddings
explanations.body: Family parties are usually held for culturally identified special occasions. In China these include special birthdays, like celebrating the first month anniversary of a new baby’s birth or the 60th birthday of an adult. For these types of celebrations families invite relatives from near and far and prepare special dishes that are usually eaten only at these special occasions. These parties are likely to be held in the family’s home or the home of a close relative that is large enough to accommodate all the guests. Weddings also are an occasion for large family gatherings. Traditional Chinese society has many wedding rituals and party customs. These elaborate traditions were practiced less frequently in the twentieth century, because of war and internal strife that faced China in the first half of the century. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, weddings in the city remained low key and were a smaller scale than the large gatherings of the past, which were still common in many parts of the countryside. Today, with China’s economic reforms, increased stability and growing wealth, weddings are again becoming larger and more complex. Some couples have traditional Chinese weddings, some follow Western ceremonies, and some do both!

explanations.title: Business receptions and conclusion
explanations.body: Business receptions and dinners are another sort of party. A foreign businessman or businesswoman may receive an invitation from a senior representative of a Chinese company who will host a dinner or evening reception to which the businessperson is invited. These invitations might also include a reference to attire and even the end time for the function, particularly if it is a reception and not a dinner. Some large enterprises or manufacturing corporations in China also host parties to celebrate their success or any positive changes that occur in their business and the surrounding community. These firms will post announcements on their public bulletin boards to tell their employees where and when to go for the celebration. They also may use invitation letters or even faxes and phone calls to invite local officials to participate as well. In conclusion, Chinese culture shares a link to Western culture in the use of parties and invitations to celebrate significant cultural events. Even though the holidays, foods and customs are unique to China, the activity is one common to the whole world. While formal invitations are less popular in China today than in the West, businesspeople, academics and other professionals who travel to China may well receive a formal dinner, banquet or even a party invitation from a firm or government organization’s representative that they work with. References: “Chinese Festivals and Events” (chinahighlights.com); “Cultural Atlas-China Etiquette” (culturalatlas.sbs.com.au).
